Trent Alexander Boult (born 22 July 1989) is a New Zealand cricketer who was born in Rotorua. He is a left arm fast medium bowler and a right-handed batter. In first-class cricket, Boult played for Northern Districts from 2008 to 2022. Since then, he has specialised in Twenty20, and has played for several franchise teams. In international cricket, he has played for New Zealand in all formats of cricket since 2011. His last international match to date (October 2025) was a Twenty20 International (T20I) in June 2024. In all, he has played in 78 Test matches, 114 One Day Internationals, and 61 T20Is. In his Test career, he has taken 317 wickets at an average of 27.49 runs per wicket.

Gregory Marasciulo (born March 30, 1987) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) under the ring name Trent Beretta. He is a member of the Don Callis Family stable. He has also made appearances in the World Wrestling Entertainment / WWE, New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Pro Wrestling Guerrilla (PWG), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), and Ring of Honor (ROH) (before AEW's purchase). Marasciulo has won many championship throughout his career. In Dragon Gate USA, he was a one-time Open the United Gate Champion. In NJPW, he was a four-time IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champion, one-time NEVER Openweight 6-Man Tag Team Champion, and the winner of the Super Jr. Tag Tournament with Rocky Romero in 2016. On February 7, 2019, Beretta and Chuck Taylor both announced that they had signed contracts with All Elite Wrestling (AEW). At Double or Nothing, Beretta would make his in-ring AEW debut. He would team with his Best Friends teammate Chuck Taylor and they defeated the team of The Hybrid2 (Angélico and Jack Evans). Best Friends would compete in a tournament to determine who would become the very first AEW World Tag Team Champions. They competed for a bye in the first round at All Out but lost to The Dark Order (Evil Uno and Stu Grayson). They would still compete in the tournament but would lose in the first round to eventual champions SoCal Uncensored (Frankie Kazarian and Scorpio Sky) on the October 16 episode of Dynamite. On the November 6 episode of Dynamite, Beretta made his AEW in-ring singles debut in a loss to Pac. At Bash at the Beach, Best Friends competed in a four-way number one contender match against The Elite (Adam Page and Kenny Omega), The Young Bucks (Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson), and The Inner Circle (Santana and Ortiz). The match was won by The Elite. They won a title shot and challenged Page and Omega for the titles on Night 1 of Fyter Fest but lost. On the April 3, 2024 episode of Dynamite, Baretta and Orange Cassidy lost a semi-final match to The Young Bucks (Matthew and Nicholas Jackson) in the tournament to crown the new AEW World Tag Team Champions. After the match, Best Friends went for their signature ringpost hug but during it, Baretta hit Cassidy with a running knee strike, turning heel, and breaking the stable up. On the May 29 episode of Dynamite, Beretta joined the Don Callis Family. On the July 13 episode of Collision, Beretta was written off television after Cassidy hit him in the back of the head with a monkey wrench. It was announced that Beretta had to have surgery to fix two broken screws in his neck.

Trent Frederic (born February 11, 1998) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins. Before playing in the NHL, Frederic played parts of two seasons with U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Wisconsin Badgers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Badgers, he was named the Big Ten Freshman of the Year adn was also named to both the All-Big Ten Freshman Team and All-Big Ten Second Team. He was drafted 29th overall by Boston Bruins in the 2016 NHL entry draft. On March 13, 2018, Frederic signed a three-year, $3.4125 million entry-level contract to join the Bruins. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. On January 29, 2019, Boston called him up and Frederic made his NHL debut in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Winnipeg Jets. On January 23, 2021, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Charlie Coyle goal in a 6–1 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On February 21, Frederic scored his first NHL goal against Carter Hart in a 7–3 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On August 1, 2023, Frederic signed a two-year, $4.6 million to stay with the Bruins. On March 4, 2025, Frederic was involved in a three-team trade with the New Jersey Devils and Edmonton Oilers. The Bruins traded Frederic to the Devils in exchange for Petr Hauser. The Devils then traded Frederic to the Oilers in exchange for Shane Lachance. On June 27, Frederic signed an eight-year, $30.8 million contract to stay with the Oilers.

Trevor Francis (19 April 1954 – 24 July 2023) was an English footballer. He has played for England national team. Francis died of a heart attack at his home near Marbella, Spain, on 24 July 2023. He was 69. Scores and results list England's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Francis goal. Football League Second Division runner-up: 1971–72 American Conference Central Division: 1978 PFA First Division Team of the Year: 1976–77, 1977–78, 1981–82 Coppa Italia top scorer: 1984–85 (9 goals) Premier League Manager of the Month: December 1993

Trevor John Linden, OBC (born April 11, 1970, in Medicine Hat, Alberta) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey player. He played centre and right wing with four different teams: the Vancouver Canucks (two different times), New York Islanders, Montreal Canadiens, and Washington Capitals. Before he joined the NHL in 1988, Linden helped the Medicine Hat Tigers of the Western Hockey League (WHL) win the Memorial Cup, the trophy for junior hockey teams in Canada, twice in a row. Linden also played for Canada at the 1998 Winter Olympics. From 1990 until 1997 Linden was the captain of the Canucks. He helped the team reach the Stanley Cup Finals in 1994.

Trevor Letowski (born April 5, 1977 in Thunder Bay, Ontario) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey right winger who played in the National Hockey League with the Phoenix Coyotes, Vancouver Canucks, Columbus Blue Jackets and the Carolina Hurricanes.

Trevor Daniel Johansen (born March 30, 1957 in Thunder Bay, Ontario) is a retired professional ice hockey player who played 286 games in the National Hockey League. Johanssen was drafted with the 12th overall pick in the 1977 NHL Entry Draft by the Toronto Maple Leafs. In addition the Maple Leafs he also spent time with the Colorado Rockies, and Los Angeles Kings.

William Theodore Mueller (born September 10, 1980) is an American professional wrestler. He is currently signed to National Wrestling Alliance (NWA) and competes under the ring name Trevor Murdoch. He is also known for his time in Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW), World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) and Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA). While in WWE as Trevor Murdoch, he was known for his tag team with the late Lance Cade. In ECW and NWA:TNA, he went by the ring name Stan Dupp and was a member of the stable, The Dupps. In TNA, he used the ring name Jethro Holiday. He is a two-time NWA Worlds Heavyweight Champion and a three-time WWE World Tag Team Champion with Cade. NWA Worlds Heavyweight Championship (2 times) NWA Champions Series Tournament (2021) – with Team Pope/Sky (Jax Dane, Jennacide, The Masked Mystery Man, and Colby Corino) Ranked No. 75 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500 in 2022 WildKat Sports Heavyweight Championship (1 time) WLW Tag Team Championship (3 times) - with Bull Schmitt (1) and Wade Chism (2) World Tag Team Championship (3 times) - with Lance Cade
Trevor James Morgan (born 30 September 1956) is a British professional athlete and coach. He is best known as an association football player. Morgan played over 400 games in his career.

Trevor van Riemsdyk (born July 24, 1991) is an American ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, van Riemsdyk played 29 games of high school hockey at the Christian Brothers Academy in Lincroft, New Jersey. He then played 2 years with New Hampshire Junior Monarchs of the Eastern Junior Hockey League (EJHL) and 3 years with the New Hampshire Wildcats. He was impressive enough in his sophomore year to be named to the 2012-13 All-Hockey East First Team. On March 24, 2014, the Chicago Blackhawks signed van Riemsdyk to a two-year entry-level deal. On October 9, 2014, he made his NHL debut in a 3–2 shootout win against the Dallas Stars. His brother James van Riemsdyk also plays in the NHL for the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Trevor Rodney Kidd (born March 29, 1972) is a Canadian former NHL goaltender who last played for the Hannover Scorpions in the Deutsche Eishockey Liga. Throughout his 12-year National Hockey League career, Kidd played for the Calgary Flames, Carolina Hurricanes, Florida Panthers and Toronto Maple Leafs. A first-round draft pick, Kidd was selected 11th overall by the Flames in the 1990 NHL entry draft.

Trevor John Cherry (23 February 1948 – 29 April 2020) was an English footballer and manager. He played as a defender. Cherry was born in Huddersfield. He played for Huddersfield Town, Leeds United and Bradford City. He made a total of 27 international caps for the England national team. He was the third England international to be shown a red card. He later managed Bradford City from 1982 to 1987. While he was manager, Valley Parade, Bradford's home ground, was the scene of a fire. 56 people died, with at least 265 injured. Cherry died on 29 April 2020 at the age of 72.

Trevor George McMahon (8 November 1929 – 12 March 2026) was a New Zealand cricketer. He played 5 tests for New Zealand in the 1955/56 season. He played for Wellington in the Plunket Shield. He was born in Wellington, New Zealand. McMahon died on 12 March 2026 in Wellington at the age of 96.

Trevor Andrew Bauer (Born January 17, 1991) is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Diablos Rojos del México of the Mexican League. He previously played for the Arizona Diamondbacks, Cleveland Indians, Cincinnati Reds, and the Los Angeles Dodgers of Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Yokohama DeNA BayStars of Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB). Bauer was the third pick in the 2011 MLB Draft. In 2020, he won the National League Cy Young Award, and was also given All-MLB First Team honors. Bauer has been an All-Star once.

Trevor Gillies (born January 30, 1979) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 5 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and New York Islanders. Outside of the NHL, Gillies also played for the Vityaz Chekhov of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) and HIFK of the SM-liiga. Gillies was known as a physical player and tended to fight often. He was known for his horseshoe moustache during his time with the Islanders. Before playing in the NHL, Gillies played parts of two seasons with the North Bay Centennials, one season with the Sarnia Sting, and two seasons with the Oshawa Generals. He was not drafted by an NHL team. He played a season with the Mississippi Sea Wolves of the ECHL. He spent most of his early career playing between multiple teams in the ECHL and the American Hockey League (AHL). On July 20, 2004, Gilles signed a contract to join the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. He played 49 games with the Wolf Pack and recorded 2 assists. On August 23, 2005, the Rangers traded Gillies along with a 2007 conditional draft pick to the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim in exchange for Steve Rucchin. On November 6, 2005, Gillies made his NHL debut in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Minnesota Wild. On July 27, 2006, Gillies signed a contract extension to stay with the Mighty Ducks. On July 2, 2007, Gillies signed a one-year contract to join the Carolina Hurricanes. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Albany River Rats. On September 14, 2009, Gillies signed with the New York Islanders AHL-affiliate Bridgeport Sound Tigers of the AHL. Gillies managed to earn 123 penalty minutes in 18 games with the Tigers. On January 28, 2010, Gillies signed with the New York Islanders. On March 14, 2010, Gillies recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Tim Jackman goal in a 4–1 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On January 13, 2011, Gillies scored his first NHL goal against Robin Lehner in a 6–4 loss against the Ottawa Senators. Gillies faced a couple suspensions after he elbowed Pittsburgh Penguins player Eric Tangradi in the face, punched him when he was down on the ice, and then taunted him from the hallway of the dressing room. The league suspended Gillies nine games for this. After returning from suspension, Gillies immediately got ejected for an illegal hit on Minnesota Wild player Cal Clutterbuck. The league suspended him for ten games because of this after an in-person hearing took place. On October 31, 2011, the Islanders placed Gilles on waivers and he was cleared o play for the Bridgeport Sound Tigers again. On June 19, 2012, Gillies decided to leave North America after he signed a one-year contract to play for Vityaz Chekhov of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He played 24 total games with the team. On August 28, 2013, Gillies signed a contract to play for HIFK of the SM-liiga. He only played 3 regular season games before the HIFK terminated his contract. He decided to head back to North America after signing a contract to join the Adirondack Flames of the AHL. On October 10, 2014, Gillies was suspended for twelve games after he smashed the face of Rochester Americans player William Carrier into the ice. On September 18, 2015, Gillies signed a one-year contract to join the South Carolina Stingrays of the ECHL. He played parts of three seasons with the Stingrays. On August 28, 2018, Gillies announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Trevor Moore (born March 31, 1995) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs. Before playing in the NHL, Moore played two seasons with the Tri–City Storm of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four years with Denver Pioneers of National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Pioneers, he was named NCHC Forward of the Year and was also named to both the NCHC All-Rookie Team and NCAA Second All-American Team. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On July 26, 2016, Moore signed a three-year, $5.325 million entry-level contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. On December 23, 2018, the Leafs called him up and Moore made his NHL debut in a 5–4 overtime win against the Detroit Red Wings. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Frédérik Gauthier goal. On January 5, 2019, Moore scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 5–0 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On January 13, 2019, Moore signed a two-year, $1.55 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On February 5, 2020, the Leafs traded Moore along with a 2020 third-round draft pick, and a 2021 conditional third-round draft pick to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Jack Campbell and Kyle Clifford. On July 24, 2021, Moore signed a two-year, $3.75 million contract to stay with the Kings. On November 16, 2022, Moore recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 3–1 win against the Edmonton Oilers. On December 15, 2022, Moore signed a five-year, $21 million contract to stay with the Kings.
Trey Lewis (born May 23, 1985 in Topeka, Kansas) is an NFL football player. He plays defensive tackle for the Atlanta Falcons. Lewis began playing for the Falcons in 2007.

Trey Anthony Lyles (born November 5, 1995) is a Canadian professional basketball player. He is a power forward/small forward for the Sacramento Kings of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He has also played for the Utah Jazz, Denver Nuggets, San Antonio Spurs, and the Detroit Pistons. Lyles played college basketball with the University of Kentucky Wildcats from 2014 until 2015. Lyles had originally committed to play for Indiana but he decommitted in August 2012. He did not play in Kentucky's six-game exhibition series in Nassau, Bahamas because of a leg injury. Lyles was drafted by the Utah Jazz in the first round with the 12th overall pick in the 2015 NBA Draft. The Jazz signed him to rookie scale contract on July 7, 2015. On January 14, 2016, Lyles was able to score a season-high 19 points in a 103-101 loss to the Sacramento Kings.

Howard Samuel "Trey" Thompkins III (born May 29, 1990) is an American professional basketball player. He plays for Real Madrid of the Liga ACB in Spain. He is listed as tall and he plays in the power forward position. He has also played for the Los Angeles Clippers (2011–2013) and Russian side Nizhny Novgorod (2014–2015). On March 12, 2020, during the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic, it was announced that Thompkins had tested positive to COVID-19.

Joseph Anthony "Trey" Mancini III (born March 18, 1992) is an American professional baseball first baseman and outfielder for the Baltimore Orioles of Major League Baseball (MLB). He made his MLB debut in 2016. His nickname Boomer. He was born in Winter Haven, Florida. On April 28, 2020 Mancini revealed he had stage 3 colon cancer.

Trifon Marinov Ivanov (; 27 July 1965 – 13 February 2016) was a Bulgarian international footballer. He played as a defender. Ivanov played his first game for Bulgaria in 1988. He earned 76 caps and scored 6 goals over a ten-year international career. He played in the 1994 and 1998 FIFA World Cups, as well as the 1996 UEFA European Championship. Ivanov died of a heart attack on 13 February 2016 in Samovodene, Bulgaria. He was aged 50. Scores and results list Bulgaria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Ivanov goal. Paul Michael Levesque (born July 27, 1969) is an American business executive, retired professional wrestler, actor, and former bodybuilder. He is better known by the ring name Triple H, an abbreviation of his former Hunter Hearst Helmsley name. He is currently the CCO ("Chief Content Officer") of WWE. Before joining WWE, Levesque began his wrestling career with World Championship Wrestling (WCW) in 1993, wrestling under the name Terra Ryzing. He would then be repackaged as Jean-Paul Lévesque, a French Canadian aristocrat, before joining World Wrestling Federation (now WWE) in 1995. During his time in WWE, he was a 14-time world champion: a nine-time WWE Champion and a five-time World Heavyweight Champion In addition, he won the 1997 King of the Ring, the 2002 Royal Rumble, and was the second Grand Slam Champion. He married Stephanie McMahon in 2003, becoming the son-in-law of WWE chairman Vince McMahon. Outside of wrestling, Levesque has made many guest appearances in film and on television. He is starring in the upcoming WWE Film Journey of Death. At the 2008 edition of Backlash, Triple H won the WWE Championship. He lost the title at Survivor Series 2008 to Edge. At the 2009 No Way Out, Triple H won back the WWE Championship in an Elimination Chamber match for the 8th time, beating The Rock's record of 7 times. After entering the 2016 Royal Rumble match at no. 30, he eliminated Ambrose to win the Royal Rumble and become a 14 time world champion. He later lost the title to Roman Reigns at WrestleMania 32. In September 2021, Triple H had heart failure and doctors put an ICD in his chest during surgery. On March 25, 2022, he officially announced his retirement from in-ring competition. On the second night of WrestleMania 38, he left his wrestling boots in the ring which was a sign of retirement. Patricia Anne Stratigias (born December 18, 1975) is a Canadian professional wrestler, yoga instructor and former fitness model. She is signed to WWE, under the ring name, Trish Stratus. Stratus is a former one-time WWE Hardcore Champion, seven-time WWF/E Women's Champion and was named Babe of the Year from 2001 to 2004 and was also named Diva of the Decade. She returned to the WWE on February 20, 2011 after she made a surpise appearance at the 2011 Elimination Chamber pay-per-view. She also was a trainer on the 2011 revival of Tough Enough. She was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame by Stephanie McMahon in 2013. The next year, Stratus inducted Lita in the Hall of Fame. Tristram E. Speaker (April 4, 1888 - December 8, 1958), was an American baseball player. He was one of the greatest center fielders in baseball history, both on offense and defense. He had a.345 career batting average (fourth all-time), and the record for most career doubles, with 792. He played 22 seasons in Major League Baseball, with the Boston Americans/Red Sox, Cleveland Indians, Washington Senators, and Philadelphia Athletics. He also was the manager of the Indians from 1916 to 1926. Speaker was born in Hubbard, Texas on April 4, 1888. Speaker, who retired from baseball in 1928, was chosen for the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1937. His induction ceremony was held in 1939. Speaker died of a heart attack in Lake Whitney, Texas on December 8, 1958. He was on a fishing trip with a friend when he died.

Tristan Trevor James Thompson (born March 13, 1991) is a Canadian-Jamaican and American basketball player for the Cleveland Cavaliers. He won the NBA championship with the Cavaliers in 2016. Thompson has also played for the national team of Canada, the Boston Celtics, Sacramento Kings, Indiana Pacers, Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Lakers. He began dating Khloé Kardashian in 2016. They have two children together. It was revealed that Thompson had cheated on Kardashian during her first pregnancy. They split in 2021.

Trischa Zorn (born June 1, 1964, in Orange, California) is an American Paralympic swimmer. Born blind, she took part in Paralympic swimming (S12, SB12, and SM12 disability categories). She is the most successful athlete in the history of the Paralympic Games, having won 55 medals (41 gold, 9 silver, and 5 bronze), and was added into the Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2012. She took the Paralympic Oath for athletes at the 1996 Summer Paralympics in Atlanta. Zorn studied special education at the University of Nebraska. She competed in the 1980, 1984, 1988, 1992, 1996, 2000 and 2004 Paralympic Games and won a combined total of 55 medals (41 gold, 9 silver, 5 bronze). In the 1996 Games in Atlanta, she won more medals than any other athlete: two gold, three silver and three bronze. She had also increased the individual medal table at the 1992 Paralympic Games in Barcelona, with ten gold medals and two silver. She had won seven gold medals during her first game in 1980. After the Sydney Games in 2000, she also held eight world records in her disability category. On 1 January 2005, Zorn was one of eight athletes admired during New Year celebrations in Times Square in New York City. The other seven were Ian Thorpe of Australia, Nadia Comăneci of Romania, George Weah of Liberia, Françoise Mbango Etone of Cameroon, Gao Min of China, Félix Sánchez of the Dominican Republic and Bart Conner of the United States.

Tristan Luneau (born January 12, 2004) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the San Diego Gulls of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is a prospect for the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Luneau played three seasons with the Gatineau Olympiques of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Olympiques. He was awarded the Raymond Lagacé Trophy as the QMJHL's defensive rookie of the year, the RDS Cup as the QMJHL's rookie of the year, and the Emile Bouchard Trophy as the QMJHL's defenceman of the year. He was also named to both the All-Rookie Team and First All-Star Team. He was drafted 53rd overall by the Anaheim Ducks in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On September 5, 2023, Luneau signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Ducks. On October 19, 2023, Luneau made his NHL debut in a 3–2 loss against the Dallas Stars. On November 22, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Mason McTavish goal in a 4–3 loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On November 30, Luneau scored his first NHL goal against Darcy Kuemper in a 5–4 loss against the Washington Capitals.

Tristen Nielsen (born February 23, 2000) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Colorado Eagles of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is under contract with the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Nielsen played parts of four seasons with the Calgary Hitmen and three seasons with the Vancouver Giants of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On July 1, 2023, Nielsen signed an two-year entry-level contract to join the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Abbotsford Canucks. He never played a game for the Vancouver Canucks. On August 1, 2025, Nielsen signed a one-year contract to join the Colorado Eagles of the American Hockey League (AHL). On October 27, Nielsen signed a one-year contract to join the Colorado Avalanche. On November 4, 2025, the Knights called him up and Nielsen made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On February 4, 2026, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Cale Makar goal in a 1–0 win against the Chicago Blackhawks.
Triston Andrew McKenzie (born August 2, 1997) is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Cleveland Guardians of Major League Baseball (MLB). He made his MLB debut in 2020.

Triwulan (born 1934) was a female Indonesian sprinter from Malang. Her main achievements were between 1950 and 1953. She was a small but had a good style. At the age of 16 years old Triwulan won the 100 metres event at the 1950 PASI athletics competitions in a time of 13.3 seconds. As a preparation for the 1951 Asian Games she went with the national team on a training camp in Djokja in January 1951. Afterwards she was selected for the Games to compete in the 100 metres and 4x 100 metres relay. Ahead of the Games, she was named as a favorite to win a medal. Still 16 years old, she was the youngest athlete at the Games. At the 1951 Asian Games she was eliminated in the heats of the 100 metres, finishing last in her heat. She won with the relay team the bronze medal in the 4x 100 metres event behind Japan and India. Triwulan won after the Games in Indonesia several tournaments and competitions in the 100 metres, including at the 1951 National Sports Week. She continued competing in the later years, with her last main competition being the 1953 National Sports Week.

Troy Hudson (born March 13, 1976, in Carbondale, Illinois) is an American former professional basketball player. He played parts of 11 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA). He played for the Utah Jazz, Los Angeles Clippers, Orlando Magic, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Golden State Warriors. He played at the point guard position.

Troy Brouwer (born August 17, 1985 in North Delta, British Columbia, Canada) is a former Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He played in the National Hockey League for the Chicago Blackhawks, Florida Panthers, Calgary Flames, St. Louis Blues and Washington Capitals. He also played in the WHL for the Moose Jaw Warriors for five seasons and was named team captain his last season with the Warriors. On June 9, 2010, Brouwer won the Stanley Cup with the Chicago Blackhawks. On Nov. 18, 2021, he retired from the NHL after a 14-year career. He won the Bob Clarke Trophy (WHL leading scorer) in 2006. He was named to the AHL Second All-Star Team in 2007. He was named to the AHL All-Rookie Team in 2007. He won the Stanley Cup in 2010. (Chicago Blackhawks)

Troy Fitzgerald Brown (born July 2, 1971) is an American football coach and former wide receiver. He is the wide receivers and kick returners coach for the New England Patriots of the National Football League (NFL).

Troy Norman Murray (July 31, 1962 – March 7, 2026) was a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He played in the National Hockey League (NHL). He was the colour analyst on WGN 720 radio broadcasts of Chicago Blackhawks hockey games. Murray was born in Calgary, Alberta. Murray died from cancer on March 7, 2026, at the age of 63.

Troy Nathan Terry (born September 10, 1997) is an American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Terry is a two-time All-Star, being named one in 2022 and 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Terry played one regular season game with the Indiana Ice and one season with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL), as well as, three years with the Denver Pioneers of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He helped the Pioneers when they went on a run in the NCAA Division I men's ice hockey tournament. They defeated the Michigan Tech Huskies and Penn State Nittany Lions to make it to the Frozen Four. They went on to defeat Notre Dame Fighting Irish before defeating Minnesota Duluth Bulldogs 4–3 to win the National Championship. He was named to the NCAA All-Tournament Team, NCHC Second All-Star Team, and was named a AHCA First-Team West All-American. He was drafted 148th overall by the Anaheim Ducks in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On April 7, 2018, Terry signed a three-year, $4.475 million entry-level contract to join the Ducks. On March 27, 2018, Terry made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On January 19, 2019, Terry scored his first NHL goal against Mackenzie Blackwood and recorded a point after assisting on a Derek Grant goal in a 3–2 win against the New Jersey Devils. On July 14, 2020, Terry signed a three-year, $4.35 million contract to stay with the Ducks. On January 4, 2022, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–1 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On January 18, Terry was selected to play in his first All-Star game. On January 05, 2023, he was selected to play in his second All-Star game. On August 2, Terry signed a seven-year, $49 million contract to stay with the Ducks.

Troy Stecher (born April 7, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Vancouver Canucks, Detroit Red Wings, Los Angeles Kings, Arizona Coyotes, Calgary Flames, and Edmonton Oilers. Before playing in the NHL, Stecher played three seasons with the Penticton Vees of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and three years with the North Dakota Fighting Hawks of the Ontario Hockey League (NCHC). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On April 13, 2016, Stecher signed a three-year, $925,000 entry-level contract to join the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. On October 25, 2016, the Panthers called him up and Stecher made his NHL debut in a 3–0 loss against the Ottawa Senators. On November 5, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Daniel Sedin goal in a 6–3 loss against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On November 13, Stecher scored his first NHL goal against Kari Lehtonen in a 5–4 overtime win against the Dallas Stars. On July 20, 2018, Stecher signed a two year, $4.65 million contract to stay with the Canucks. On October 10, 2020, Stecher signed a two-year, $3.4 million contract to join the Detroit Red Wings. He played two seasons with the Wings. On March 20, 2022, the Red Wings traded Stecher to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for a 2022 seventh-round draft pick. He played two seasons with the Wings. He recorded 1 assist in 13 regular season games and also scored 2 goals and recorded 2 assist in 4 playoff games with the Kings. On July 13, 2022, Stecher signed a one-year, $1.25 million contract to join the Arizona Coyotes. He recorded 7 assists in 61 regular season games with the Coyotes. On March 3, 2023, the Coyotes traded Stecher along with Nick Ritchie to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Connor Mackey and Brett Ritchie. He scored 3 goals and recorded 4 assists in 20 regular season games with the Flames. On July 1, 2023, Stecher signed a one-year, $1.1 million contract to return the Arizona Coyotes. He scored 1 goal and recorded 4 assists in 47 regular season games in his return with the Coyotes. On March 8, 2024, the Coyotes traded Stecher along with a 2024 seventh-round draft pick to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick. On July 1, Stecher signed a two-year, $787,500 contract to stay with the Oilers. On November 15, 2025, the Oilers placed Stecher onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Toronto Maple Leafs the same day. On June 30, 2026, Stecher signed a two-year, $2.7 million contract to stay with the Leafs.

Truls Carl Eric Möregårdh (born 16 February 2002) is a Swedish professional table tennis player. He won a silver medal in the men's singles event at the 2024 Summer Olympics, and at the 2021 World Table Tennis Championships. In 2025, Möregårdh became the first European to win a WTT Grand Smash singles title.

Trần Văn Nhung (1933 – 10 October 2020), also known as Pierre, was a Vietnamese footballer. He played for South Vietnam at the 1956 and 1960 AFC Asian Cups. After the 1954 Geneva Conference, he was invited to play in France, but decided not to. He was nicknamed "The Divine Horse" because of his speed. Trần Văn Nhung died on 10 October 2020, at the age of 87.

Tsanko Hantov also written as Цанко Хантов (born 11 August 1976) is a Bulgarian modern pentathlete, fencer and fencing coach. With fencing Hantov, was junior national epee champion in 1995 and 1996. He became national senior champion in 1998. In modern pentathlon he participated in the men's individual pentathlon event at the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney. The next year he won the bronze medal at the 2001 World Modern Pentathlon Championships. Htantov was a fencing coach for over seven years. He is the owner of the "Windy City Fencing", an epee fencing club in Chicago, where is also the head coach since 2005.
Tsegaye Mekonnen is a long-distance runner from Ethiopia. He was born on 15 June 1995. Mekonnen competed at the 2017 World Championships in Athletics.

Tsukasa Umesaki is a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Umesaki was born in Isahaya on February 23, 1987. He joined J1 League club Oita Trinita from their youth team in 2005. He became a regular player in 2006. In January 2007, he moved to French Ligue 2 club Grenoble. In May 2007, he returned to Oita. In 2008, he moved to Urawa Reds. He could not play many matches for injuries until 2011, he became a regular player from 2012. Urawa won the 2nd place in the 2014 and 2016 J1 League. Although his opportunity to play decreased from 2016, Urawa won the champions in 2017 AFC Champions League. In 2018, he moved to Shonan Bellmare. In 2018, Shonan won the champions J.League Cup. In September 2006, Umesaki was selected the Japan national team for 2007 Asian Cup qualification. At this qualification, he debuted against Yemen on September 6. In July 2007, he was selected the Japan U-20 national team for 2007 U-20 World Cup. At this tournament, he played all 4 matches as left midfielder and scored a goal against Scotland in the first match.

Tsukasa Hosaka was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Hosaka was born in Kofu on March 3, 1937. After graduating from Meiji University, he joined Furukawa Electric in 1959. He won 1960, 1961 and 1964 Emperor's Cup. In 1965, Furukawa Electric joined new league Japan Soccer League. He retired in 1968. He played 47 games in the league. In November 1960, he was selected by the Japan national team for the 1962 World Cup qualification. At this qualification, on November 6, he debuted against South Korea. In 1962, he also played at the Asian Games. He was a regular goalkeeper in the early 1960s. In 1964, he was selected by Japan for the Summer Olympics in Tokyo. However, he did not play in the match, because he fractured his hand just before the Olympics. Instead, he was the team's reserve goalkeeper behind Kenzo Yokoyama. He played 19 games for Japan until 1964. After retirement, Hosaka became a manager for his local club Kofu SC in 1973. He managed until 1977. On January 21, 2018, Hosaka died of pneumonia in Kofu at the age of 80.

Tsukasa Shiotani is a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Shiotani was born in Komatsushima on December 5, 1988. After graduating from Kokushikan University, he joined J2 League club Mito HollyHock in 2011. He played many matches as center back from first season. In August 2012, he moved to J1 League club Sanfrecce Hiroshima. From 2013, he played many matches as right back of three back defense with Kazuhiko Chiba and Hiroki Mizumoto. Hiroshima won the J1 League champions in 2012, 2013 and 2015. He was also selected Best Eleven in 2014, 2015 and 2016. In June 2017, he moved to UAE Pro League club Al-Ain. On October 10, 2014, Shiotani debuted as center back for the Japan national team against Jamaica. In 2016, he was also selected the Japan U-23 national team as over aged player for 2016 Summer Olympics. He played all 3 matches as center back with Naomichi Ueda. In 2019, he participated 2019 Asian Cup. He played 5 matches as defensive midfielder and 1 goal, Japan won the 2nd place. Tsukasa Morishima is a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Morishima was born in Mie Prefecture on April 25, 1997. After graduating from Yokkaichi Chuo Technical High School, he joined J1 League club Sanfrecce Hiroshima in 2016. He played many matches from 2019. In December 2019, Morishima was selected the Japan national team for 2019 E-1 Football Championship. At this tournament, he debuted against China on December 10.

Tsuneyasu Miyamoto is a former Japanese football player and manager. He played for the Japan national team. Miyamoto was born in Tondabayashi on February 7, 1977. He joined J1 League club Gamba Osaka from their youth team in 1995. He became a regular player as center back from later 1990s. He also served as a captain. He played 295 matches for the club in 12 seasons. In 2005, the club won the champions J1 League. In 2007, he moved to Austrian Bundesliga club Red Bull Salzburg. In January 2009, he returned to Japan and signed with Vissel Kobe. He retired end of the 2011 season. Miyamoto played for Japan U-17 national team in the 1993 U-17 World Championship and Japan U-20 national team in the 1997 World Youth Championship. He played full-time in all matches in both tournaments. In September 2000, he was also selected the Japan U-23 national team for 2000 Summer Olympics. On June 18, 2000, Miyamoto debuted for Japan national team against Bolivia. As a center back, he served as captain for Japan in the 2002 World Cup, after an injury to Ryuzo Morioka, who had begun the tournament as captain. He then continued to captain his country through the 2004 Asian Cup and the 2006 World Cup. At 2004 Asian Cup, he played full-time in all 6 matches and Japan won the champions. At 2006 World Cup, he played the first two group matches of the cup, but was suspended for the third and last match against Brazil after he received yellow cards against Australia and Croatia. Yuji Nakazawa wore the armband in his place. This competition was his last game for Japan. He played 71 games and scored 3 goals for Japan until 2006. After the retirement, Miyamoto started coaching career at Gamba Osaka in 2015. He became a manager for Gamba Osaka U-23 in 2017. In July 2018, top team manager Levir Culpi was sacked when the club was at the 16th place of 18 clubs. Miyamoto was named new manager as Culpi successor. Miyamoto raised Gamba to the 9th place in 2018 season. In 2020, the club won the 2nd place in J1 League and Emperor's Cup. Austrian Bundesliga: 2007; runner-up: 2008

Tsuyoshi Kitazawa is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Kitazawa was born in Machida on August 10, 1968. After graduating from Shutoku High School, he joined Japan Soccer League club Honda in 1987. He was the top scorer of the league in the 1990–91 season. He moved to Yomiuri (later Verdy Kawasaki, Tokyo Verdy) in 1991. The club won the league champions in 1991–92 and 1991 JSL Cup. In 1992, Japan Soccer League was folded and the club joined new league, J1 League. Kitazawa, together with his teammates Kazuyoshi Miura, Ruy Ramos, Nobuhiro Takeda, Tetsuji Hashiratani and Bismarck made in the early 1990s the golden era of Verdy who won the J1 League championship (1993 and 1994) and J.League Cup (1992, 1993, and 1994). He finished his playing career as a Verdy player in 2002. Kitazawa was capped 58 times and scored 3 goals for the Japan national team between 1991 and 1999. He made his international debut on June 2, 1991 in a friendly against Thailand, under national manager Kenzo Yokoyama. He was a member of the Japan team for the 1992 Asian Cup that Japan won. He took part in Japan's unsuccessful campaign to qualify for the 1994 World Cup. He was a member of the Asian final qualification stage that was held centrally in Doha and played two games. He was on the bench when the Iraqi's injury-time equaliser dashed Japan's qualification hope in the last qualifier, in the match that the Japanese fans now remember as the "Agony of Doha" (ドーハの悲劇). Kitazawa was short-listed for the 1998 World Cup, but national manager Takeshi Okada dropped him along with Kazuyoshi Miura and Daisuke Ichikawa at the final training camp in Nyon, Switzerland. Kitazawa represented Japan national futsal team in the 1989 Futsal World Championship hosted by the Netherlands.

Tsuyoshi Kunieda is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Kunieda was born in Hiroshima Prefecture on September 18, 1944. After graduating from Chuo University, he joined his local club Toyo Industries in 1967. The club won Japan Soccer League champions in 1967, 1968 and 1970. The club also won 1967, 1969 Emperor's Cup. He retired in 1972. He played 38 games and scored 3 goals in the league. In October 1969, Kunieda was selected the Japan national team for 1970 World Cup qualification. At this qualification, on October 16, he debuted against Australia. On October 18, he also played against South Korea. He played 2 games for Japan in 1969.

Tsutomu Sonobe is a former Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Sonobe was born in Ibaraki Prefecture on March 29, 1958. After graduating from Mito Commercial High School, he joined Japan Soccer League club Fujita Industries in 1976. The club won the league champions in 1977, 1979 and 1981. The club also won 1977 and 1979 Emperor's Cup. He retired in 1989. He played 173 games and scored 2 goals in the league. He was selected Best Eleven in 1978 and 1979. On May 23, 1978, Sonobe debuted for the Japan national team against Thailand. He played 7 games for Japan until 1981.

Tsunekazu Takeda is a Japanese athlete. He is best known as an Equestrian who competed in two Summer Olympic Games. He is the current President of the Japanese Olympic Committee. Takeda was born on November 1, 1947 in Tokyo. He was the third son of Prince Tsuneyoshi Takeda and his great-grandfather was Emperor Meiji. He graduated from Keio University in 1970 with a degree in law. Takeda was a member of the Japanese team in the 1972 Summer Olympics at Munich and the 1976 Summer Olympics at Montreal. He was a competitor in the All Japan Equestrian Championships in 1969, 1975, 1977, 1978 and 1982. In 2001, he became president of the Japanese Olympic Committee. He is also an Executive Board member on the Olympic Council of Asia. In July 2012, he was elected to be a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

Tsuyoshi Yamanaka was a Japanese freestyle swimmer. He won a total of five Olympic medals, four silvers and a bronze. He won medals at the 1956 (Melbourne), 1960 (Rome) and 1964 Summer Olympics (Tokyo). He was born in Wajima, Ishikawa Prefecture. Yamanaka died from pneumonia on 10 February 2017 in Tokyo, at the age of 78.

Tsuru Morimoto is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Her father Mamoru Morimoto is former middle distance runner. Morimoto was born on November 9, 1970. She played for Nissan FC. However, the club was disbanded in 1993. After she left the club, she played for Nikko Securities Dream Ladies and the Ladies side of Italian Serie A club Lazio. On August 21, 1994, Morimoto debuted and scored a goal for the Japan national team against Austria. She was a member of Japan for 1995 World Cup. She also played at 1994 Asian Games and 1995 AFC Championship. She played 5 games and scored 1 goal for Japan until 1995.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is a Japanese football player who plays as a defender for Belgian First Division A club Gent. Watanabe was born in Saitama Prefecture on February 5, 1997. After graduating from Chuo University, he joined J1 League club FC Tokyo in 2019. He played many matches as center back from first season. In December 2019, Watanabe was selected the Japan national team for 2019 E-1 Football Championship. At this tournament, he debuted against Hong Kong on December 14.

Tu'u Maori (22 November 1988 – 4 January 2022) was a Papua New Guinea international rugby league footballer. He played as a wing or center. He played in the Australian National Youth Championship for the Cronulla Sharks and Sydney Roosters. He played for the Papua New Guinea national rugby league team in 2008. Maori died from motor neurone disease in Auckland, New Zealand on 4 January 2022, at the age of 33.

Tuba Hassan is a cricketer from Pakistan. She plays for the Pakistan women's national cricket team. She was born on October 18, 2000. She is the first Pakistani cricketer to win ICC Women's Player of the month award in 2022.

Tugay Kerimoğlu (born 24 August 1970) is a former Turkish football player. He has played for Turkey national team. 1.Lig: 1987–88, 1992–93, 1993–94, 1996–97, 1997–98, 1998–99 Turkish Cup: 1990–91, 1992–93, 1995–96, 1998–99 Turkish Super Cup: 1988, 1991, 1993, 1996, 1997 Blackburn Rovers Player of the Year: 2003–04
Tumi Sphindile Sekhukhune is a cricketer from South Africa. Sekhukhune plays for the South Africa women's national cricket team. She was born on November 21, 1998.

Tunch Ilkin (born Tunç Ali İlkin; September 23, 1957 – September 4, 2021) was a Turkish-born American football player and sports broadcaster. He played as an offensive tackle for the Pittsburgh Steelers and Green Bay Packers. He was the first Turk to play in the National Football League (NFL). After his playing career, he was a television and radio analyst for the Steelers from 1998 to 2020. His career lasted from 1980 until 1993. Ilkin was born in Istanbul, Turkey. In October 2020, Ilkin announced that he was living with ALS. He died from the disease on September 4, 2021 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, at the age of 63.

Tuomas Oskar Grönman (born 22 March 1974 in Viitasaari, Finland) is a Finnish retired professional ice hockey defenceman. He played 2 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) with the Chicago Blackhawks and Pittsburgh Penguins organizations. He also played in the SM-Liiga for TPS, Lukko and Jokerit. He won a bronze medal with Team Finland at the 1998 Winter Olympics.

Kaiho Tuomas Albin Gerdt (28 May 1922 – 1 November 2020) was a Knight of the Mannerheim Cross. Gerdt, serving as a junior runner officer in the infantry regiment 7, was awarded the Mannerheim Cross on 8 September 1942. At that time he held the rank of a Sergeant. After coming home from the war on 13 November 1944, Gerdt worked as a manager in Oy Wilh. Schauman Ab and as an office manager in Oy Kaukas Ab and Kymmene Oy. He was born in Heinävesi, Finland. Gerdt, serving as the chairman of the Mannerheim Cross Knight Foundation, is the last living Knight of the Mannerheim Cross. Gerdt died on 1 November 2020 in Helsinki at the age of 98.

Walter Edward “Turk” Broda (May 15, 1914 – October 17, 1972) was a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender for the Toronto Maple Leafs. He was born in Brandon, Manitoba on May 15, 1914 to a Polish-Canadian family. He joined the Maple Leafs in 1936. Broda stepped away from hockey from 1943 to 1946 so he could fight in World War II. He returned to the Leafs in 1946. NHL First All-Star Team Goalie (1941 & 1948) Stanley Cup Championships (1942, 1947, 1948, 1949, & 1951) Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1978 In 1998, he was ranked number 60 on The Hockey News list of the 100 Greatest Hockey Players “Honoured Member” of the Manitoba Hockey Hall of Fame Inducted into the Manitoba Sports Hall of Fame and Museum in 1983

Turgay Sabit Şeren (15 May 1932 – 6 July 2016) was a Turkish footballer. He was the former goalkeeper of Galatasaray. He played at Galatasaray between 1947 and 1966 and was capped 52 times for Turkey, including two matches at the 1954 FIFA World Cup. Şeren was awarded a testimonial match by the club in 1967 in Istanbul.

Turkey has been in 6 UEFA European Championships (1996, 2000, 2008, 2016, 2020 and 2024). Their best performance was reaching the semi-finals in 2008.
