Edey plays for the Canada men's national basketball team. He played for them during the 2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup where Canada would win a bronze medal. Before playing in the NHL, Bogosian played parts of two seasons with the Peterborough Petes of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the teams. He finished his rookie season with 7 goals and 26 assists for 33 points. He was named to the Second All-Rookie Team. The next season, he was chosen to participate in the CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game and was named to the First All-Star Team. He was drafted 3rd overall by the Atlanta Thrashers in the 2008 NHL entry draft. On September 4, 2008, Bogosian signed a three-year, $2.625 million entry-level contract to join the Thrashers. On October 10, Bogosian made his NHL debut in a 7–4 win over with the Washington Capitals. On January 17, 2009, Bogosian recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Colby Armstrong goal. He then scored his first NHL goal against Pekka Rinne in a 7–4 win over with the Nashville Predators. On October 31, 2009, Bogosian broke his thumb and hurt his wrist when a teammate fell on his arm. He didn't miss any playing time but it affected his play and caused his production to fall. He stayed with the team when they relocated to become the Winnipeg Jets. On September 14, 2011, Bogosian signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Jets. On February 26, 2008, the Jets traded Bogosian along with Evander Kane and Jason Kasdorf to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Tyler Myers, Drew Stafford, Brendan Lemieux, Joel Armia, and a 2015 first-round draft pick. He played parts of six seasons with the Sabres. On February 21, 2020, the Sabres placed Bogosian on unconditional waivers to terminate his contract. On February 23, 2020, Bogosian signed a one-year, $1.3 million contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning. He helped the Lightning when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Florida Panthers, Carolina Hurricanes, and New York Islanders. They went on to defeat the Montreal Canadiens four games to one in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On October 10, 2020, Bogosian signed a one year, $1 million contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs. He recorded 4 points in his only seasons with the Leafs. On July 28, 2021, Bogosian signed a three-year, $2.55 million contract to rejoin the Tampa Bay Lightning. He played parts of three seasons after rejoining. On November 8, 2023, the Lightning traded Bogosian to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for a 2025 seventh-round draft pick. He played parts of three seasons after rejoining. Bogosian is married to former professional football player Bianca D'Agostino.

Zachary L'Heureux (born October 28, 1995) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Nashville Predators. Before playing in the NHL, L'Heureux played one season with the Moncton Wildcats and three seasons with the Halifax Mooseheads of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was drafted 27th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On July 28, 2021, L'Heureux signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On October 22, 2024, the Predators called him up and L'Heureux made his NHL debut in a 4–0 win against the Boston Bruins. On October 26, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Alexandre Carrier goal in a 4–3 overtime win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On November 17, L'Heureux scored his first NHL goal against Kevin Lankinen in a 5–3 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On March 18, 2026, L'Heureux signed a two-year, $1.75 million contract to stay with the Predators. On June 24, 2026, the Predators traded L'Heureux along with Fedor Svechkov to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for Chase Bradley, Jack Drury, and a 2029 third-round draft pick.

Zack Ostapchuk (born May 29, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators. Before playing in the NHL, Ostapchuk played five seasons with the Vancouver Giants and one season with the Winnipeg Ice of the Western Hockey League (WHL). On March 8, 2022, the Giants named Ostapchuk as their new captain. He was drafted 39th overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On September 29, 2021, Ostapchuk signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Belleville Senators. On March 12, 2024, Ottawa called him up and Ostapchuk made his NHL debut in a 2–1 overtime win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On October 29, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Noah Gregor goal in a 2–1 overtime win against the St. Louis Blues. On January 28, Ostapchuk scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 2–1 win against the New Jersey Devils. On March 7, 2025, the Senators traded Ostapchuk along with Noah Gregor and a 2025 second-round draft pick to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Tristen Robins, Fabian Zetterlund, and a 2025 fourth-round draft pick.

Zachary Martin Hyman (born June 9, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger and children's author. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs. As an author, Hyman released the books The Bambino and Me, Hockey Hero, and The Magician's Secret. He won the Blue Spruce Award in 2019. Before playing in the NHL, Hyman played parts of four years with the Michigan Wolverines of the Central Collegiate Hockey Association (CCHA) and Big Ten Conference (B1G). He finished the 2014–15 season scoring 22 goals and recording 32 assists for 54 points in 37 regular season games. He was named the Big Ten Scoring Champion, and was named to the All-Big Ten First Team, Big Ten All-Tournament Team, and as an AHCA West First-Team All-American. He was drafted 123rd overall by the Florida Panthers in the 2010 NHL entry draft. He never played a game for the Panthers. On June 19, 2015, the Panthers traded Hyman's rights to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for centre Greg McKegg and a 2017 conditional seventh-round draft pick. On June 23, Hyman signed a two-year, entry-level contract to join the Leafs. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. On February 29, 2016, the Leafs called him up and Hyman made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On March 7, Hyman scored his first NHL goal against Chad Johnson in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Buffalo Sabres. On July 5, 2017, Hyman signed a four-year, $9 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On July 28, 2021, Hyman signed a seven-year, $38.5 million contract to join the Edmonton Oilers. Hyman is also an award-winning children's author and works under Penguin Random House. He released The Bambino and Me in 2014, Hockey Hero in 2015, and The Magician's Secret in 2018. He was awarded a starred Kirkus Review for The Bambino and Me in 2014 and also won a Blue Spruce Award for The Magician's Secret in 2019.

Zachary Kenneth Werenski (born July 19, 1997) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. Werenski is a one-time James Norris Memorial Trophy winner, winning in 2024. He is also a -time All-Star, being named one in 2018 and 2022. Internationally, Werenski plays for the United States and won a gold medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Werenski played one season with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Michigan Wolverines of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was named the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year and was named to the All-Big Ten Freshman Team, back-to-back All-Big Ten First Teams, and the Big Ten All-Tournament Team. He was also named a AHCA West First-Team All-American. He was drafted 8th overall by the Columbus Blue Jackets of the 2015 NHL entry draft. On March 29, 2016, Werenski signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Jackets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Lake Erie Monsters. On October 13, 2016, the Jackets called him up and Werenski made his NHL debut in a 6–3 loss against the Boston Bruins. During the first period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Alexander Wennberg goal. Two days later on October 15, Werenski scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Martin Jones in a 3–2 loss against the San Jose Sharks. On December 31, 2019, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–1 win against the Florida Panthers. On July 29, 2021, Werenski signed a six-year, $57.5 million contract to stay with the Jackets. On June 2, 2026, Werenski was awarded the James Norris Memorial Trophy.

Zach Whitecloud (born November 28, 1996) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. He has also played for the Vegas Golden Knights. Whitecloud is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Golden Knights in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Whitecloud played one regular season game with the Portage Terriers and three seasons with the Virden Oil Capitals of the Manitoba Junior Hockey League (MJHL), as well as, two years with the Bemidji State Beavers of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Beavers, he was named to the WCHA All-Rookie Team. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 8, 2018, Whitecloud signed an three-year, $4.475 million entry-level contract to join the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). On April 5, 2018, Whitecloud made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Edmonton Oilers. After the game he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. He played two seasons with the Wolves before being called back up. On February 28, 2020, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Reilly Smith goal in a 4–2 win against the Buffalo Sabres. During a Stanley Cup Qualifiers round-robin game on February 7, 2021, Whitecloud scored his first NHL goal against Jordan Binnington in a 6–4 win against the St. Louis Blues. On March 22, 2020, Whitecloud signed a two-year contract to stay with the Knights. On October 28, 2021, Whitecloud signed a six-year, $16.5 million contract to stay with the Knights. He helped the Knights during the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Dallas Stars. They went on to defeat the Florida Panthers four games to one in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Golden Knights franchise history. On January 18, 2026, the Knights traded Whitecloud along with Abram Wiebe, a conditional 2027 first-round draft pick, and a 2028 conditional second-round draft pick to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Rasmus Andersson. Whitecloud was born in Brandon, Manitoba and is of Dakota descent. He spent much of his time in the Sioux Valley Dakota Nation.

Zack MacEwen (born July 8, 1996) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Vancouver Canucks, Philadelphia Flyers, Los Angeles Kings, Ottawa Senators, and New Jersey Devils. Before playing in the NHL, MacEwen played two seasons with the Moncton Wildcats and one season with the Gatineau Olympiques of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 3, 2017, MacEwen signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. On February 11, 2019, the Canucks called him up and MacEwen made his NHL debut in a 7–2 win against the San Jose Sharks. During the third period, he recorded his fist NHL point after assisting on a Derrick Pouliot goal. On December 3, MacEwen scored his first NHL goal against Anders Nilsson in a 5–2 win against the Ottawa Senators. On October 6, 2020, MacEwen signed a two-year contract to stay with the Canucks. On October 13, 2021, the Canucks placed MacEwen onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Philadelphia Flyers. On August 2, 2022, MacEwen signed a one-year contract to stay with the Flyers. He scored seven goals and recorded 11 assists over two seasons with the Flyers. On March 3, 2023, the Flyers traded to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Brendan Lemieux and a 2024 fifth-round draft pick. He recorded an assist in 10 regular season games with the Kings. On July 6, 2023, MacEwen signed a three-year, $2.325 million contract to join the Ottawa Senators. On November 28, the league fined MacEwen $2,018 for unsportsmanlike conduct against Florida Panthers player Matthew Tkachuk during a game. On October 3, 2025, the Senators traded MacEwen to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Kurtis MacDermid. He played three regular season games with the Devils. On July 1, 2026, MacEwen signed a two-year, $1.75 million contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Mir Zafarullah Khan Jamali (Urdu/Baloch: میر ظفراللہ خان جمالی) (January 1, 1944 – December 2, 2020) was a Pakistani politician and businessman. He was the 15th Prime Minister of Pakistan from 2002 to 2004. He was the chairman of the Pakistan Hockey Federation. Mir Zafarullah Khan Jamali was born in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan. Jamali died of a heart attack on December 2, 2020 in Rawalpindi, Pakistan at the age of 76.

José Alves, nicknamed Zague (August 10, 1934 – January 19, 2021) was a Brazilian footballer. He played for Corinthians in his home country, and Club América in Mexico. Alves died on January 19, 2021 at the age of 86.

Zafar Sobhan (born 1970) is a Bangladeshi businessman, editor and former football player. He started the Dhaka Tribune newspaper. He runs a news company. Sobhan is the first Bangladeshi news writer to be syndicated outside Bangladesh. This means that newspapers from other countries paid to put his writing in their papers. Sobhan was also a senior editor at the Daily Star newspaper and an editor of Forum magazine. He wrote for The New York Times, The Guardian, TIME, and other newspapers and magazines. His news company is the 2nd most famous in Bangladesh and Dhaka behind Daily Star As of 21 December 2022 he is still active. The World Economic Forum named him a Young Global Leader in 2005. It named him an Asia 21 Young Leader in 2008. He married S.F.A. Sobhan on Thanksgiving 2011. They have three children: Shamil, Suri, Azfar.

Zachary Harrison Wheeler (born May 30, 1990) is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Philadelphia Phillies of Major League Baseball (MLB). He has also played in MLB for the New York Mets. Wheeler was born to a baseball-playing family in Smyrna, Georgia. He moved to Dallas, Georgia, shortly before the start of high school. There, he pitched for East Paulding High School. He led the team to a state playoff appearance in 2009. He pitched a no-hitter against Mill Creek High School. The San Francisco Giants chose Wheeler sixth overall in the 2009 MLB Draft. He decided to sign with the team rather than go to Kennesaw State where he had planned to play baseball. Wheeler played for the Giants' minor league teams in 2010 and 2011. He was traded to the Mets in July 2011. Wheeler then rose through the Mets' farm system. He first played in the major leagues in 2013. Wheeler's tore his ulnar collateral ligament during spring training in 2015. He had Tommy John surgery for the injury. The Mets thought he would return during the 2016 season. He did not return until 2017 because of problems during his rehabilitation. Wheeler became a free agent at the end of the 2019 season. He signed a five-year deal with the Phillies in December 2019. In his tenure with the Phillies, Wheeler has become the team's ace (best pitcher). He has had a below 3.00 ERA in five of his six seasons with the team. He was named an All-Star in 2021, 2024, and 2025. Zachary Harrison Wheeler was born on May 30, 1990, in Smyrna, Georgia. He was raised in Dallas, Georgia, by Barry and Elaine Wheeler. Wheeler's father played amateur baseball for 15 years. His mother playing softball even after having children. She would put a playpen in the dugout during weekend games. Zack was the youngest of three brothers. They all grew up playing baseball. His oldest brother, Jacob, stopped playing sports in high school after he had surgeries for supraventricular tachycardia. His middle brother, Adam, was a minor league pitcher in the New York Yankees farm system until he torn his glenoid labrum. The Wheeler family moved to Dallas, Georgia, when Zack was 13 years old. Wheeler attended East Paulding High School, where he played baseball and basketball. As a junior in 2008, Wheeler had an 8–3 win–loss record, with a 1.31 earned run average (ERA) and 127 strikeouts in innings pitched. He was named the Georgia High School Association 4A Region Pitcher of the Year. The next year, he set a school record with 149 strikeouts in 76 innings. He had a 9–0 record and 0.54 ERA. Wheeler was named the Gatorade Georgia Player of the Year. As a designated hitter, Wheeler also had a batting average of.280 during his senior year. During the second round of 2009 Class 5A state playoffs, Wheeler pitched his first no-hitter, against Mill Creek High School. In 2015, East Paulding retired Wheeler's No. 45 jersey. His middle brother, Adam, was a minor league pitcher in the New York Yankees farm system until he torn his glenoid labrum. The Wheeler family moved to Dallas, Georgia, when Zack was 13 years old. Wheeler attended East Paulding High School, where he played baseball and basketball. As a junior in 2008, Wheeler had an 8–3 win–loss record, with a 1.31 earned run average (ERA) and 127 strikeouts in innings pitched. He was named the Georgia High School Association 4A Region Pitcher of the Year. The next year, he set a school record with 149 strikeouts in 76 innings. He had a 9–0 record and 0.54 ERA. Wheeler was named the Gatorade Georgia Player of the Year. As a designated hitter, Wheeler also had a batting average of.280 during his senior year. During the second round of 2009 Class 5A state playoffs, Wheeler pitched his first no-hitter, against Mill Creek High School. In 2015, East Paulding retired Wheeler's No. 45 jersey. The San Francisco Giants of Major League Baseball (MLB) chose Wheeler in the first round of the 2009 MLB Draft. He was the sixth pick in the draft. At the time, he had planned to play college baseball at Kennesaw State. On August 17, 2009, Wheeler signed with the Giants. His deal included a $3.3 million signing bonus. The Giants put Wheeler on their Class A Augusta GreenJackets team in the South Atlantic League to start the 2010 season. He was placed on the disabled list early in the year. He had a fingernail injury on the middle finger of his throwing hand. Wheeler was sent to San Francisco to see the team's hand doctor. He later returned to the GreenJackets. There he made several relief appearances before re-entering the starting rotation. In 21 games with Augusta, including 13 starts, Wheeler posted a 3–3 record and a 3.99 ERA, with 70 strikeouts in innings. He also played in the 2010 All-Star Futures Game in Anaheim, California. Before the 2011 season, Baseball America named Wheeler the number two prospect in the Giants organization. They said that he had the "best fastball" in the farm system. He was assigned to the Class A-Advanced San Jose Giants. He went 7–5 with a 3.99 ERA and 98 strikeouts in 16 starts and 88 innings pitched. He also played in the 2011 California League All-Star Game. On July 28, 2011, the Giants traded Wheeler to the New York Mets. The Giants received veteran outfielder Carlos Beltrán and cash. Giants general manager Brian Sabean said that they chose to trade Wheeler because, "[w]e didn't think (Zack) Wheeler was going to impact our situation in the immediate future. Quite frankly, it's our job to find another Wheeler or develop another Wheeler." He spent the rest of the season with the Class A St. Lucie Mets. There he went 2–2 with a 2.00 ERA and 31 strikeouts in 27 innings across six starts. The Mets assigned Wheeler to the Double A Binghamton Mets of the Eastern League at the start of the 2012 season. He became the best player in that season's Binghamton pitching rotation. He struck out 25 percent of batters he faced. This led the Eastern League. In 116 innings and 19 starts, Wheeler went 10–6 with Binghamton. He gave up only two home runs. He was named an Eastern League All-Star. Wheeler also received his second All-Star Future Game selection. On July 14, 2012, Wheeler pitched his first professional complete game shutout in a 1–0 victory over the Erie SeaWolves. The next day, the Mets said that he was not being considered for a major league promotion. On July 31, he struck out 11 batters in a game against the Harrisburg Senators. The next day the Mets moved Wheeler to the Triple-A Buffalo Bisons. Many Mets pitchers had injuries that year. They decided to have their young pitchers pitch fewer innings. They decided Wheeler should only pitch 150 innings that year. On September 1, he threw five innings against the Lehigh Valley IronPigs. The Mets did not let him pitch anymore in 2012. In 149 innings between Binghamton and Buffalo, Wheeler had a 12–8 season record with a 3.26 ERA. He led Minor League Baseball with 148 strikeouts. Mets general manager Sandy Alderson told reporters that Wheeler would probably start the 2013 season with Buffalo. He also said Wheeler would probably play his first major league game that same year. The Buffalo Bisons decided to be the Toronto Blue Jays' Triple-A team during the 2012 offseason. Wheeler and other Mets Triple-A pitchers began pitching in 2013 for the Las Vegas 51s of the Pacific Coast League. This league was known at the time for being good for hitters but hard for pitchers. Wheeler had a rough start to the season. He had a 6.34 ERA in his first three starts with Las Vegas. He pitched well in his fourth game. He struck out eight batters in innings against the Reno Aces on April 30. With Las Vegas that season, Wheeler had a 4–2 record with a 3.93 ERA and 73 strikeouts in innings and 13 starts. Wheeler played in his first major league game on June 18, 2013. He pitched six shutout innings in the second game of a doubleheader against the Atlanta Braves. Wheeler had seven strikeouts and gave up four hits in the 6–1 win. On August 15, Wheeler struck out a career-high 12 batters in a 4–1 win over the San Diego Padres. He became the youngest Mets pitcher to record at least 12 strikeouts in a game since Doc Gooden in 1986. On September 21, the Mets ended his season. This was because he felt shoulder stiffness in his last game. Wheeler finished his first season with a 7–5 record, a 3.42 ERA, and 84 strikeouts in 100 innings in 17 starts. Matt Harvey would miss the 2014 season to recover from Tommy John surgery. Some sports writers thought Wheeler would become the Mets' ace. His pitching did not always pitch well in the first two months of the season. He had a large number of walks. He had poor record against left-handed batters. On June 19, 2014, Wheeler pitched a complete-game shutout against the Miami Marlins. He only faced 28 batters and allowed just three hits. The Mets' 2014 season was thought of as disappointing. They did not make the playoffs. Wheeler's pitching was considered to be a good part of the season. He had an 11–11 record that season, with a 3.54 ERA and 187 strikeouts in innings in 32 starts. On March 16, 2015, the Mets said that Wheeler had torn the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow. The injury was found after he began having pain during spring training. People reported that Wheeler had torn a tendon in the same elbow during the previous season. They said that he had platelet-rich plasma therapy to heal his elbow better. Wheeler had Tommy John surgery for the torn ligament on March 25. The Mets hoped Wheeler would return to the team in July 2016. Wheeler had problems in his return from Tommy John surgery. In early April 2016, he had a second surgery. This was to take out a undissolved stitch in his elbow. The Mets moved his expected return to after the MLB All-Star break. In late June, he felt pain in his elbow again. Finally, in mid-August, the Mets ended his season. Doctors said he had a strained flexor tendon. It needed another plasma injection. On September 3, Mets manager Terry Collins told reporters that Wheeler would not pitch anymore in 2016. Wheeler signed a one-year, $800,000 contract with the Mets on January 11, 2017. He made his first major league start in over two years on April 8. He allowed five runs and six hits in only four innings against the Miami Marlins. Wheeler had a good first inning with his fastball speeds up to 97 mph. His speed dropped to 93 mph as the game continued. The worst two starts of his career both happen in June. First, he gave up eight runs in innings against the Chicago Cubs. Then he gave up two home runs to Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Cody Bellinger. Wheeler was put on the 10-day disabled list on June 22 with biceps tendinitis. He had been feeling soreness in the arm since a June 7 start against the Texas Rangers. Some sports writers wondered if he should have been pitching in those games. Injuries continued to happen to Wheeler through the second part of the season. He returned to the disabled list on July 24 after suffering an injury to the humerus. The met season on August 24. In 17 starts, Wheeler posted a 3–7 record with a 5.21 ERA for the 2017 season. Wheeler was healthy to start the 2018 season. The Mets signed All-Star Jason Vargas in the offseason. People thought that Wheeler would be moved out of the starting rotation and into the bullpen because of this. He did not pitch well in spring training. Wheeler began the season in the minor leagues in Las Vegas. Vargas was injured early in the season. Wheeler took his spot on the Mets. He had a good game against the Washington Nationals on April 18. This showed he could stay with the Mets. His pitching was especially good after the All-Star break. He led MLB in WHIP with 0.81 and had the second-lowest ERA with 1.32. By mid-September, the Mets thought about ending his season early. His innings pitched were more than two times his 2017 total. Mets manager Mickey Callaway said on September 19, 2018, that Wheeler would not pitch anymore that year. He went 12–7 for the year, with a 3.31 ERA and a 1.12 WHIP in 29 starts. Wheeler was set to become a free agent at the end of the 2019 season. People thought that the Mets would try to trade Wheeler before the July 31 deadline. They chose to keep him. General manager Brodie Van Wagenen told reporters, "We think he's a good pitcher. We have interest in him being a Met for the long term." Like in 2018, Wheeler was better in the second half of 2019. He had a 4.69 ERA in the first part of the season. Then he allowed only one earned run in each of his final five starts. Wheeler also had the most innings pitched and strikeouts (195) in his career. He finished the season with an 11–8 record and a 3.96 ERA in 31 starts. On December 9, 2019, the Philadelphia Phillies signed Wheeler as a free agent to a five-year, $118 million contract. He played his first game for them in a 7–1 victory against the Miami Marlins on July 25, 2020. This was less than a week after the birth of his son Wesley. On September 9, Wheeler's fingernail ripped from nail bed while he was trying to put on a pair of jeans. A week later, he pitched with a fake fingernail. He had surgery for the injury on October 12. The 2020 season was short because of the COVID-19 pandemic. He had a 4–2 record and 2.92 ERA in 11 games and 71 innings. He led the NL in batters hit by pitch with 7. He was the first Phillies pitcher to allow three or fewer runs in each of his first 10 starts with the team. He allowed only three home runs. That was the fewest of any pitcher in 2020 who pitched at least 70 innings. In his first 2021 game, Wheeler struck out 10 batters in 7 innings. He became the first Phillies' pitcher to have two or more hits and RBIs in a game since Ben Lively in 2017. On May 29, Wheeler struck out a career-high 14 batters. He was the third pitcher in Phillies history, following Steve Carlton and Curt Schilling, to strike out 10 or more batters in three starts in a row. He had a 2.05 ERA in his first 17 starts. He led the league with 139 strikeouts in 114 innings pitched. Wheeler received his first MLB All-Star Game selection because of his good first part of the season. Some fans thought that Wheeler would be chosen to start for the National League team, but Max Scherzer of the Nationals was the starter. Wheeler pitched at the top of the ninth inning to strike out Matt Olson and end the inning. Wheeler led MLB with a career-high innings. He finished the season 14–10 with a 2.78 ERA. He also had league-leading three complete games, two shutouts, and 849 batters faced. He struck out 247 batters. He was first Phillies pitcher to win the NL strikeout title since Curt Schilling in 1998. Wheeler finished second in NL Cy Young Award voting behind Corbin Burnes. He was named a finalist for the 2021 NL Gold Glove Award at pitcher. It was won by Max Fried. In 2022, he was 12–7 with a 2.82 ERA in 153 innings with 163 strikeouts over 26 starts. His career 0.812 home runs-per-9 innings was the 4th-lowest among active major league pitchers. His salary of $26 million was the 10th-highest of all NL baseball players. In 2023, his ERA went up to 3.61, but his win-loss record improved to 13–6. He struck out 212 batters in 192 innings. He won his first Gold Glove Award. He mostly used his four-seam fastball (44% of the time) and slider (27%), while also mixing in a sinker and curveball. On March 4, 2024, Wheeler signed a three-year, $126 million contract extension with the Phillies. In 2024, he was 16–7 with a 2.57 ERA in 200 innings with 224 strikeouts over 32 starts. He finished second in NL Cy Young voting for the second time. Chris Sale won the award. On June 9, 2025, Wheeler struck out Kyle Tucker in the sixth inning. This was Wheeler's 1,000th career strikeout as a Philadelphia Phillie. He became the 10th player in team history to reach 1,000 strikeouts as a Phillie. In July 2025, Wheeler decided not to play in the 2025 All-Star Game at Truist Park in Atlanta. He said that he would "rather just get [himself] ready to go for the second half" of the season even though "it would be an honor to throw [or] start." On August 16, Wheeler was placed on the injured list. He had a blood clot near his right shoulder. On August 23, doctors said he had venous thoracic outlet syndrome. He decided to have season-ending thoracic outlet decompression surgery. Wheeler finished his 2025 season with a 10–5 record, a 2.71 ERA, and 195 strikeouts (a league-high mark at the time of his injury). Wheeler uses five pitches. These include a four-seam fastball, a sinker, a curveball, a slider, and a changeup. Baseball experts think Wheeler's four-seam fastball is his best pitch. In 2019, his average fastball speed was 96.8 mph. This was much higher than the MLB average of 93.4 mph. His sinker is also known for its speed. In the 2020 season, Wheeler's sinker speed of 97.1 mph was the second-highest among pitchers who threw the pitch at least 100 times. Wheeler began to use his fastball more as he got older. This is because batters made contact more often against the sinker. New York Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole did the same thing. Cole's did better when he used his sinker less. Wheeler thinks his curveball is "decent." He thinks that his control of the pitch has gotten worse as his slider has gotten better. His changeup is a pitch Wheeler began throwing in the 2014 season. He uses it to confuse batters who think he is going to throw a hard fastball. His slider is the pitch he thinks he has to work on the most. Wheeler said before the 2021 season that he wanted to be more consistent in throwing it. He wanted to "make it look like a strike instead of it... being like a waste pitch". Wheeler and his wife Dominique have four children. They have a son born July 20, 2020. They also have three daughters. They reside in Dallas, Georgia during the offseason. Wheeler has a close friendship with retired Atlanta Braves player Chipper Jones. The two were introduced when Jones' agents met with Wheeler in high school.

Zachery Stortini (born September 11, 1985) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey right winger. He currently works as an assistant coach with the Tucson Roadrunners of the American Hockey League (AHL). He played parts of 6 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Edmonton Oilers and Nashville Predators. Before playing in the NHL, Stortini played parts of three seasons with the Sudbury Wolves of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Wolves, playing 247 regular season games with them and becoming their long-serving captain. He was drafted 94th overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 2003 NHL entry draft. On September 15, 2004, Stortini signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Oilers. On January 20, 2007, Stortini made his NHL debut in a 4–0 loss against the Calgary Flames. He was sent down to play for the Oiler's AHL-affiliate Hamilton Bulldogs where he won the Calder Cup with them. He was later called back up. On February 6, Stortini scored his first NHL career goal against Roberto Luongo in a 5–2 loss against the Vancouver Canucks. Oh July 15, 2008, Stortini signed a three-year contract to stay with the Oilers. On July 5, 2011, Stortini signed a one-year, two-way contract to join the Nashville Predators. He only played 1 game with the team before being sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On July 7, 2013, Stortini signed to a one-year, two-way contract to join the Anaheim Ducks but never played for them. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Norfolk Admirals. He played 73 games with the Admirals, scoring 4 goals and recording 5 assists. On July 2, 2014, Stortini signed a one-year, two-way contract to join the Philadelphia Flyers but once again never played for them. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Lehigh Valley Phantoms. On July 1, 2015, Stortini signed a two-year, two-way contract to join the Ottawa Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Senators and served as their captain. On January 24, 2017, the Senators traded Stortini along with Buddy Robinson and a 2017 seventh-round draft pick in exchange for Tommy Wingels. On July 5, 2017, Stortini decided to stay in the AHL and signed a one-year contract to join the Charlotte Checkers. He was able to win his second Calder Cup with the team. On September 20, 2017, Cole signed a one-day contract to return to the Carolina Hurricanes and announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey. He decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey in 2019. On August 17, 2022, Stortini was hired to become an assistant coach for the Tucson Roadrunners of the AHL.

Zaira Orellana (born 3 May 1989) is a Mexican volleyball player. She played at the 2006 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship, 2006 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup, 2007 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup, 2008 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup, 2009 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup, 2010 Women's Pan-American Volleyball Cup, 2011 Women's NORCECA Volleyball Championship, 2013 Women's NORCECA Volleyball Championship, 2014 FIVB World Grand Prix, 2014 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship, and 2015 FIVB World Grand Prix. She played for Jalisco.

Zakhar Romanovich Bardakov (; born 24 February 2001) is a Russian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Bardakov has also played for the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Bardakov played one season with HC Vityaz and four seasons with SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 203rd by the New Jersey Devils in the 2021 NHL entry draft. He never ended up playing for the team and continued his career in the KHL with SKA. On 1 March 2024, the Devils traded Bardakov along with a 2024 seventh-round draft pick to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for Kurtis MacDermid. On 20 April 2025, Bardakov signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Avalanche. On 18 October 2025, Bardakov made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Boston Bruins. Three days later on 21 October, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Cale Makar goal in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Utah Mammoth. On 28 October 2025, Bardakov scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 8–4 win against the New Jersey Devils. After the season, he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Colorado Eagles. He played 1 regular season game with them. On 3 July 2026, Bardakov decided to return to Russia and signed a one-year contract to rejoin SKA Saint Petersburg with his rights still held by the Avalanche.

Zakir Hussain Allarakha Qureshi (9 March 1951 – 15 December 2024) was an Indian tabla player, composer, percussionist, music producer and movie actor. He was known for playing classical Indian music. He was honored with the National Endowment for the Arts' National Heritage Fellowship. Hussain has received seven Grammy Award nominations, with four wins, including three in 2024. Hussain died on 15 December 2024 at his home in San Francisco, California from problems caused by idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis at the age of 73.

Zamira Myrzabekova (born 12 June 1991) is a Kazakhstani female water polo player. She competed for the Kazakhstan women's national water polo team in the 2010 Asian Games, 2015 World Aquatics Championships, 2017 World Aquatics Championships, and 2019 World Aquatics Championships.
Zanne Smit (born 3 March 2001) is a South African water polo player. She competed for the South Africa women's national water polo team in the 2019 World Aquatics Championships.

Zandre Smit Mimica (born 2 October 1998) is a South African water polo player and coach. She competed for the South Africa women's national water polo team in the 2017 World Aquatics Championships she is also a renowned netball player who was crucial in South Africa’s first ever silver medal in international fast 5 netball competition held in New Zealand in 2022.

Zane Edward Green (born 11 October 1996) is a Namibian cricketer who was born in Windhoek. He is a left-handed batter, and a wicket-keeper. Green has played in One Day Internationals (ODIs) and Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is) for Namibia since 2019.

Zane McIntyre (né Gothberg; born August 20, 1992) is an American professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Straubing Tigers of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League (NHL) and the Dinamo Riga of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, McIntyre played parts of 2 seasons with the Fargo Force of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and 3 years with the Bemidji State Beavers. He was drafted 165th overall by the Boston Bruins in the 2010 NHL entry draft. On June 23, 2015, McIntyre signed a two-year entry-level contract with the Bruins. He was sent down and played most of his time with their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. He was called up after Tuukka Rask suffered a groin injury. On October 25, 2016, McIntyre made his NHL debut in a 5-0 loss against the Minnesota Wild. On July 14, 2017, McIntyre signed a two-year; $650,000 contract extension to remain with the Bruins. During his time with the Bruins, he played 8 games and went 0-4. On July 1, 2019, McIntyre signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Vancouver Canucks. He never played a game with them and spent his time with their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. On October 14, 2019, the Canucks called McIntyre up to the NHL but he didn't play with them. On February 24, 2020, the Canucks traded McIntyre to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Louis Domingue. He was sent down to their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Devils. He only played 4 games with them before leaving. On October 26, 2020, McIntyre left North America and traveled to Latvia after signing a contract to play for Dinamo Riga of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He only played 6 games with them before ending his contract. On December 27, 2020, he returned to North America after signing a professional tryout with the Arizona Coyotes. On January 18, 2021, he joined the Lehigh Valley Phantoms after being released from the Coyotes training camp. He played 19 games with them. On January 4, 2022, McIntyre signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Minnesota Wild. He was assigned to their AHL-affiliate Iowa Wild and played 3 seasons with them. On July 11, 2024, McIntyre traveled to Germany after signing a one-year contract with the Straubing Tigers of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL).

Zane Moosa (born 23 September 1968) is a South African former footballer who played at both professional and international levels as a midfielder. Moosa played club football in South Africa and Saudi Arabia for Wits University, Mamelodi Sundowns, Avendale Athletico, Al-Ahli and Kaizer Chiefs; he also earned five caps for the South African national side between 1992 and 1996. He was part of the squad that won the 1996 African Cup of Nations. Zane Moosa's stye of play is characterized by his exceptional football skills and his ability to perform at both professional and international levels. He played as a midfielder and was known for his tenacity and determination on the field. Moosa's career highlights include playing for clubs like Wits University, Mamelodi Sundowns, Avendale Athletico, Al-Ahli, and Kaizer Chiefs, as well as earning five caps for the South African national side. His contributions to the sport were recognized when he was part of the squad that won the 1996 African Cup of Nations. Moosa's legacy in football is marked by his performances and the impact he had on the game during his playing days. Regarded as one of the finest dribblers in South African football. Moosa began his career in 1986 with the Wits University team. In 1989, he moved to Mamelodi Sundowns. In 1990, he won the South African championship with him. In 1993, he played on loan at Avendale Athletico. Then he returned to Mamelodi, where he played until the end of the 1996/1997 season. Then he went to Saudi Al-Ahli Jeddah. In the 1997/1998 season, he won the Saudi Arabian Cup with him. In 1998, he moved to Kaizer Chiefs. In the 1998/1999 season, he won the South African vice-championship with him, after which he ended his career. Between 1992 and 1996, Moosa played 5 games for the South African national team. In 1996, he was called up to the team for the African Cup of Nations. He played there in the match against Egypt (0:1), and South Africa became the winner of the tournament. Mossa is a Muslim. His older brother Essop Moosa was also a footballer. National Soccer League: 1987–1988, 1989–90, 1992–93

Zara Anne Elizabeth Tindall (née Phillips; born 15 May 1981) is a British equestrian (horse rider) and the second-eldest grandchild of the late Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh. Tindall is the second child, and only daughter, of Anne, Princess Royal and her first husband, Mark Phillips. She is married to Mike Tindall, who used to be a rugby player for England. She is better known by her maiden name (her old name before marriage). In the line of succession, she is called "Mrs Michael Tindall". She was given an Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) honour in the 2007 New Year's Honours List, by her grandmother for her services to equestrianism. In 2012, she carried an Olympic flame at a racecourse in Cheltenham. She won a silver medal at London 2012. Tindall was born at St Mary's Hospital in London. She is the eldest granddaughter of Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh. When she was born, she was sixth in line to the throne. She is now 18th in line. She has an older brother, Peter Phillips (born 15 November 1977). She has two half-sisters, Felicity Tonkin (born in 1985 after her father had an affair) and Stephanie Phillips, born 2 October 1997, from her father's second marriage. The children of the Princess Royal do not hold a title. It is thought their mother did not want them to have one. On 21 December 2010, Buckingham Palace said she was engaged to Mike Tindall MBE. She got a diamond and platinum engagement ring from Tindall. They married in 2011. Her first daughter and child, Mia Grace Tindall, was born on 17 January 2014 at Gloucestershire Royal Hospital in Gloucestershire. Her second daughter and child, Lena Elizabeth Tindall was born on 18 June 2018 in Stroud Maternity Hospital at Stroud. A son, Lucas Philip Tindall, was born March 24, 2021 at Gatcombe Park in Gloucestershire.

Zarley Bennett Zalapski (April 22, 1968 – December 10, 2017) was a Canadian-Swiss professional ice hockey defenceman. He was born in Edmonton, Alberta. He played from 1987 to 2010. He played for the Pittsburgh Penguins, the Hartford Whalers, the Calgary Flames, the Montreal Canadiens and for the Philadelphia Flyers. Zalapski died on December 12, 2017 in Calgary, Alberta of a viral infection at the age of 49. After his death, his sister sent his brain to Toronto to be studied. Doctors said that Zalapski had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).
Zbigniew Kazimierz Boniek (born 3 March 1956) is a former Polish football player. He has played for Poland national team. Boniek is currently the vice president of UEFA.

Zbigniew Jan Pietrzykowski (4 October 1934 – 19 May 2014) was a Polish boxer. He participated in three Olympic Games. He won a medal in every game. He fought 44 times, winning 42 times and losing twice. In his career, he fought 350 fights; he won 334, drew 2 and lost 14.

Zaōnishiki Toshimasa (born Toshimasa Adachi; 3 September 1952 – 9 August 2020) was a sumo wrestler. He was born in Yamagata, Japan. He made his professional debut in September 1970, and reached the top division in November 1976. His highest rank was maegashira 1. He retired in January 1983. He became an elder in the Japan Sumo Association. He reached the retirement age for elders of 65 in September 2017. Zaōnishiki revealed in 2014 that he was diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He died on 9 August 2020 from the disease at the age of 67.

Zbigniew Pacelt (26 August 1951 – 4 October 2021) was a Polish Olympic athlete and politician. He competed as a swimmer at the 1968 and 1972 Summer Olympics, and as a modern pentathlete at the 1976 Summer Olympics. He was a member of the Sejm from 2005 until 2015. He was a member of the Civic Platform. Pacelt was born in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, Poland. Pacelt died on 4 October 2021 at the age of 70.

Zbigniew Rybak (27 March 1973 — 21 December 2022) was a Polish rugby union player. He was co-founder of RC Arka Gdynia in Gdynia and played for the club after it was founded. In 2000 he played in the documentary film of Sylwester Latkowski entitled To my, rugbiści (translated: It’s us, rugby players). (as himself), 2000, documentary directed by Sylwester Latkowski. Klatka, 2003, documentary directed by Sylwester Latkowski.

Zdeno Chára (born March 18, 1977) is a Slovak former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played a total of 24 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the New York Islanders, Ottawa Senators, Boston Bruins, and Washington Capitals. He was the captain of the Bruins from 2006 until 2020. Chára played hockey in the WHL for 1 season with the Prince George Cougars. He is the tallest player ever to play in the NHL, being 6 ft 9 (2.06 m). On March 8, 2011, He was in an on-ice incident when he hit Montreal Canadiens player Max Pacioretty into the stanchion at the end of the bench in the boards. Pacioretty had to be taken off the ice on a stretcher and he was very hurt by a large concussion and a non-displaced fracture to the 4th vertebra. Chára received a five-minute large punishment and a game misconduct. The NHL VP of hockey operations, Mike Murphy, decided that no more punishments were going to be given, even though the Montreal police said they would do criminal investigation. On September 20, 2022, Chára said that he was no longer going to play professional hockey. He retired as a member of the Bruins after signing a one-day contract with them. On 24 June 2025, Chára was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. Chára is married to his wife Tatiana Biskupicová and they have one daughter named Elliz Victoria Chára. He played in the NHL All-Star Game in 2003, 2007, 2008 (starter), 2009, 2011, and 2012. Chára was also one of the team captains in the 2012 game. He was named to the NHL First All-Star Team in 2004 and 2009. He was named to the NHL Second All-Star Team in 2006 and 2008. He won the James Norris Memorial Trophy in 2009. He won the Hardest Shot competition at the NHL All-Star Game SuperSkills Competition in 2007, 2008, 2009, and 2011 where he set a record of 105.9 mph (170.4 km/hr). He won the NHL Plus-Minus Award in 2011 with a +33 rating. He won the Stanley Cup with the Boston Bruins in 2011.

Zbyněk Michálek (born 23 December 1982) is a Czech former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played parts of 14 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Minnesota Wild, Phoenix/Arizona Coyotes, Pittsburgh Penguins, and St. Louis Blues. He was undrafted but started his career in the NHL with the Minnesota Wild. He played for the Wild for a season and mainly stayed with their farm team, Houston Aeros whom he won the Calder Cup with in 2003. He was traded to the Phoenix Coyotes for Erik Westrum and Dustin Wood in 2005. He played 5 seasons with the Coyotes and lead the league in blocked shots during the 2008–09 NHL season. He signed a 5-year, $20 million contract with the Pittsburgh Penguins on July 1, 2010. He played 2 seasons with them and was traded back to the Coyotes during Draft Day 2012 for Harrison Ruopp, Marc Cheverie and a 2012 third-round draft pick (81st overall). On 19 October 2017, Michálek signed a contract with Sparta Praha of the Czech Extraliga (ELH). He last played for Kometa Brno before retiring from playing professional ice hockey. His younger brother Milan also played in the NHL for parts of 13 seasons.

Zdzisław Myrda (29 January 1951 – 6 July 2020) was a Polish basketball player. He competed in the men's tournament at the 1980 Summer Olympics. He was born in Siedliska, Poland. Myrda died on 6 July 2020 at the age of 69.

Zdzislawa Wiszniewska-Bednarek was a Polish female basketball player and Czech handball player. She was a member of SSA Warsaw, the Poland women's national basketball team and the Poland women's national Czech handball team playing as an halfback. She competed with the national basketball team in the 1934 Women's World Games basketball tournament, where they didn't reached the final and where classified third. She represented Italy three years later at the 1937 International University Games. With the national team she won the bronze medal at EuroBasket Women 1938 in Rome, the first official women's basketball championships. With the national Czech Handball team, she also competed at the World Games in the 1934 Women's World Games Czech handball tournament. Ahead of the main tournament in London, they lost the qualifier match in Zagreb against Yugoslavia and were excluded from further competition.

Zdena Smolová also written as Zdeňka Smolová with marriage name Fleischerová (17 April 1908 - 25 November 1964) was a Czechoslovak track and field athlete during the 1920s and 1930s, the early era of women's athletics. She was world record holder. She won two silver medals and a bronze medal at the second Women's World Games in 1926 and also two bronze medals at the Olympics of Grace in 1931. Smolová was born in 1908 in Brno and was a member of AC Moravská Slavia Brno. On 12 July 1925 she set with the national team the world record in the 4 x 75 meters relay with a time of 40.2 seconds. In 1926, she represented Czechoslovakia at the 1926 Women's World Games in Gothenburg. She won the silver medal in the standing long jump event behind Japanese Kinue Hitomi and a bronze medal in the long jump event behind Hitomi and British Muriel Gunn. She won the bronze medal in the 4 × 110 yards relay together with Ludmila Sychrová, Štepánka Kucerová and Marie Vidláková. She had also other international successes, including winning the long jump at the 1926 Stockholm international women's athletics meeting and had also a podium finish in the high jump. She also competed at the 1930 Women's World Games.

Zeev Buium (born December 7, 2005) is an Israeli–American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Minnesota Wild. Before playing in the NHL, Buium played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team and two years with Denver Pioneers of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with the Pioneers. Buium finished his freshman season, scoring 11 goals and recording 39 assists for 50 points in 41 games. He was named the NCHC Rookie of the Year, NCHC Offensive Defenseman of the Year, AHCA West First Team All-American, and was named to the All-NCHC Rookie Team, All-NCHC First Team, and NCAA All-Tournament Team. He followed his freshman season with another productive year. He was named the NCHC Player of the Year and the back-to-back NCHC Offensive Defenseman of the Year, as well as, being named to the All-NCHC First Team, NCAA All-Tournament Team, and an AHCA West First Team All-American. He was drafted 12th overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On April 13, 2025, Buium signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Wild. On April 20, Buium made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Vegas Golden Knights in Game 1 of the first round in the playoffs. He became the first player in Wild franchise history to make their debut during the playoffs. On December 12, the Wild traded Buium along with Marco Rossi, Liam Öhgren, and a 2026 first-round draft pick to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for Quinn Hughes. On 4 September 2026, Buium signed a eight-year, $75.04 million contract to stay with the Canucks. Buium holds both United States and Israel citizenship. His older brother Shai is also a professional hockey player.

Edmund Raymond "Zeke" Bratkowski (October 20, 1931 − November 11, 2019) was an American professional football player. He was a quarterback in the National Football League (NFL) for fourteen seasons with the Chicago Bears, Los Angeles Rams, and Green Bay Packers. He was born in Danville, Illinois. Bratkowski died at his home in Santa Rosa Beach, Florida on November 11, 2019 of a heart attack at the age of 88.

Zemgus Girgensons (born 5 January 1994) is a Latvian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Tampa Bay Lightning of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres. Outside of the NHL, Girgensons played for Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Girgensons is a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2015. Before playing in the NHL, Girgensons played five seasons with the Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He had a successful time with the Lakers. He helped the team during the playoffs. They defeated Färjestad BK and Örebro HK. They went on to defeat Rögle BK four games to one in the Final to win Le Mat Trophy. He was also awarded the Stefan Liv Memorial Trophy for being the most valuable player of the playoffs. He was drafted 156th overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 13 July 2012, Girgensons signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Sabres. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On 2 October 2013, the Sabres called him up and Girgensons made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Detroit Red Wings. During the third period, he scored his first NHL goal against Jimmy Howard. On 10 January 2015, he was selected to play in his first All-Star game. On 1 September 2016, Holmberg signed a one-year, $1.15 million contract to stay with the Sabres. On 17 August 2017, Girgensons signed a two-year, $3.2 million contract to stay with the Sabres. On 6 July 2019, Girgensons signed a one-year, $1.6 million contract to stay with the Sabres. On 20 June 2023, Girgensons signed a one-year contract to stay with the Sabres. On 1 July 2024, Girgensons signed a three-year, $2.55 million contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Zenón Díaz (31 December 1880 – 5 September 1948) was an Argentine footballer who played as a defender for Rosario Central. He started as a goalkeeper in 1903. Later, Díaz played as a defender, becoming in one of the most famous footballer of amateur era. He played around 150 games and scored 8 goals. He won 4 national titles and 7 locals titles with the canallas. He also worked at the Central Argentine Railway. He was the first native player in Argentina national team. His first match was in 1905 versus Nottingham Forest. Later he played in several cups against Uruguay, and participated in the first South American Championship (1916). Copa Nicasio Vila (6): 1908, 1914, 1915, 1916, 1917, 1919 Copa Damas de Caridad: 1910, 1914, 1915, 1916

Zenon Plech (1 January 1953 – 25 November 2020) was a Polish international motorcycle speedway rider. He finished third in the Speedway World Championship in 1973 and as the runner-up in 1979. Plech was born in Zwierzyn, Poland. Plech died on 25 November 2020 in Gdansk, Poland at the age of 67.
Zesh Rehman or Zeshan Rehman (born 14 October 1983) is a Pakistani former football player. He has played for Pakistan national team. Scores and results are list Pakistan's goal tally first.

José Procópio Mendes, best known as Zezé Procópio (August 12, 1913 in Varginha, Minas Gerais State – February 8, 1980 in Valença, Rio de Janeiro State) is a former Brazilian football player. He has played for Brazil national team. Zezé Procópio's style of play was characterized by his robust defensive abilities and precise ball distribution. He was known for his tireless energy and strategic approach, which solidified the Brazilian team's midfield during the 1938 FIFA World Cup. Despite not scoring a goal, his performances were instrumental in Brazil's journey to the semifinals, leaving a significant mark on fans and securing his place in World Cup history. His skill and passion on the pitch made him a pivotal figure in the team's success. Commonly regarded as one of the best central midfielders in Brazilian football. He made his debut in football in 1932 playing for the Villa Nova team, in which he spent four seasons. During 1936-1938 he defended the colors of the club "Atlético Mineiro". With his play for the latter team, he attracted the attention of representatives of the coaching staff of the Botafogo club, which he joined in 1938. He played for the team from Rio de Janeiro for the next four seasons of his playing career. Subsequently, from 1942 to 1944, he played as part of the teams of the clubs Palmeiras and São Paulo. In 1945, he returned to the Palmeiras club, for which he played 3 seasons. He ended his professional career as a football player in 1948. In 1938, he made his debut in official matches as part of the national team of Brazil. During his career with the national team, which lasted 9 years, he played 20 matches in its uniform. As part of the national team, he participated in the 1938 World Cup in France, where he played against Poland (6–5), Czechoslovakia (1–1), Italy (1–2) and Sweden (4–2), and the team won bronze medals. He also participated in the 1945 South American Championship in Chile, where he won silver with the team, the 1946 South American Championship in Argentina, where he won silver with the team.

Zhang Jike (simplified Chinese: 张继科; traditional Chinese: 張繼科; born 16 February 1988 in Qingdao) is a Chinese table tennis player. He became the world champion in 2011 and 2013. In 2012 he won the Olympic Games. Zhang is the fourth man in history to win the Grand Slam. In 2006 Zhang Jike came into the National Team. After two years he become the Chinese Master in the Singles. His first World Championship that he played, was 2011 in Rotterdam. Zhang came into the final and beat Wang Hao with which he became World Champion in singles. In the same year he won the World Cup, where his opponent was Wang Hao again. He is the third player in history after Jan-Ove Waldner and Jorgen Persson, who won these important titles in one year. In 2012 Zhang Jike was nominated for the Olympic Games in London. He competed in singles as well as team competitions, where he won gold in both. From June to December 2012 he was the number 1 in the world, because he won the Olympic Games in the singles. In the final at the World Championships 2013 Zhang played against Wang Hao and defended his title after defeating him. In 2014 he won the World Cup for second time. His final-opponent was Ma Long. At the WTTC 2015 he won bronze in the singles and gold in the doubles with Xu Xin. In the semifinals in the singles category he lost to Fang Bo. During this year he lost unusually often against non-Chinese players. Nevertheless, he was nominated for the Olympic Games 2016. Here he won the silver medal in singles and with the team the gold medal. At the Asian Cup in the same year he lost to Xu Xin the final at the singles category. In the Chinese Superleague 2016 he didn't play. In 2017 he had to stop because of a fever in the second round. At the World Championships he came to Round 32 only. At the Asian Championships in the same year he came into the semifinals and won with the team the gold medal. At the China Open he lost at the Round of 32. And didn't play the year anymore. That's why in 2018 he was only ranked 78th, the lowest since 2008.

Zev Buffman (October 11, 1930 – March 31, 2020) was an Israeli Broadway producer. He was President and CEO of Ruth Eckerd Hall in Clearwater, Florida. He made more than 40 Broadway shows. He partnered with Elizabeth Taylor to present her in her Broadway debut, The Little Foxes. Buffman was also the co-founding General Partner of the NBA Champion Basketball team the Miami Heat. In 2011-2018, Buffman was named the President & CEO of Ruth Eckerd Hall. Buffman died at a hospital in Seattle of pancreatic cancer on March 31, 2020 at the age of 89.

Zhaksylyk Ushkempirov (6 May 1951 – 2 August 2020) was a light-flyweight Greco-Roman wrestler from Kazakhstan. He won an Olympic gold medal in 1980 and a world title in 1981. Ushkempirov took up wrestling in 1969 and won the Soviet title in 1975 and 1980.

Zhang Enhua (; 28 April 1973 – 29 April 2021) was a Chinese professional football player and coach. As a player, he was a defender from 1994 to 2006. He played for Dalian Wanda FC, Grimsby Town, Tianjin Teda and South China. Chinese Jia-A League: 1994, 1996, 1997, 1998, 2000, 2001, 2002

Zeteny Jano (born 13 March 2005) is an Austrian professional footballer. He plays as midfielder for Austrian Second League club Liefering. He also plays for the FC Salzburg squad in the UEFA Youth League 2021-22 and the U18 team of the Red Bull Academy. He started in Hungary with Soproni VSE and SC Sopron. 2018 he went to SC Lichtenwörth and in the same year to the Red Bull Salzburg Academy where he played in all three teams. In February 2022 he debuted for FC Liefering when he came in for Luka Reischl in minute 74 versus SKN St. Pölten. He also played five matches for FC Salzburg U19 in the UEFA Youth League 2021-22. In July 2023 he received a contract with Red Bull Salzburg until 2027. He stayed with the farm team. Jano made his debut in September 2021 against Denmark for the Austrian U-17 team. In September 2022 he made his debut versus Sweden for the U-18 team.

Zhang Lijun (born 31 August 1985) is a Chinese female Paralympic sitting volleyball player. She is part of the China women's national sitting volleyball team. She competed at the 2008 Summer Paralympics winning the gold medal, 2012 Summer Paralympics winning the gold medal, 2016 Summer Paralympics winning the silver medal, 2014 World Para Volleyball Championships, and 2018 World Para Volleyball Championships.

Zhang Yuqian (born 2 May 2000) is a Chinese volleyball player. She played for the Chinese national team. She played at the 2015 FIVB Volleyball Girls' U18 World Championship, 2016 Asian Women's U19 Volleyball Championship, and 2017 FIVB Volleyball Women's U20 World Championship. She played for Shanghai women's volleyball team.

Zhang Tonglei (born 5 September 1993) is a Chinese wheelchair basketball player. She is a member of the China women's national wheelchair basketball team and the Guangdong Province team. She won the silver medal at the 2020 Summer Paralympics, and the gold medal at the 2018 Asian Para Games. At the 2018 Women's World Wheelchair Basketball Championship she finished fourth.

Zhao Wei (born 12 March 1976), also known as Vicky Zhao or Vicki Zhao, is a Chinese actress, film director, producer and pop singer. She is considered one of the most popular actresses in China and Chinese-speaking regions, and one of the highest paid actresses. Over her 20 years acting career, Zhao has starred in many box-office smash-hits, including Shaolin Soccer (2001), Red Cliff (2008-2009), Painted Skin (2008), Painted Skin: The Resurrection (2012), Dearest (2014) and Lost in Hong Kong (2015). She has received numerous awards from the Shanghai International Film Festival, Huabiao Awards, Changchun Film Festival, Hundred Flowers Awards and Shanghai Film Critics Awards for films like A Time to Love (2005) and Mulan (2009). In 2014, after almost 2-year break from acting, she returned to the silver screen in Peter Chan's movie Dearest, and won the Hong Kong Film Critics Society Award and Hong Kong Film Award for Best Actress. Her directorial debut So Young (2013) broke the box office record for movies directed by female Chinese directors in just a week. The movie also earned her multiple awards in mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, including Golden Rooster Award for Best Directorial Debut, Hundred Flowers Award for Best Director and Hong Kong Film Award for Best Film from Mainland and Taiwan. Zhao was named as member of the main Jury at the 73rd Venice Film Festival. Zhao Wei became a Goodwill Ambassador of the United Nations Development Programme on 20 November 2016.

Zhanna Syroeshkina (born 4 June 1999 in Ekibastuz) is a Kazakhstani female volleyball player. She was part of the Kazakhstan women's national volleyball team at the 2018 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship. She played for VC Almaty in 2018.
Zhao Meiling (born 16 March 1987) is a Chinese sitting volleyball player. She played at the 2016 Summer Paralympics, winning a silver medal. and 2020 Summer Paralympics, winning a silver medal.

Zheng Zhi (; born 20 August 1980) is a Chinese professional football manager and former player. As a player, Zheng played most of his career for Chinese Super League club Guangzhou, becoming their captain and serving also as their caretaker manager in two stints. Zhivko Gospodinov (; 6 September 1957 – 4 May 2015) was a Bulgarian footballer. He was an attacking midfielder and playmaker. He played for Spartak Varna, Vatev Beloslav, Spartak Pleven, AD Fafe, Cherno More Varna and Beroe Stara Zagora from 1974 to 1992. Gospodinov was born in Vladimirovo. He died on 4 May 2015 in Varna, aged 57.

Zhou Guanyu (Chinese: 周冠宇; pinyin: Zhōu Guànyǔ, pronounced [ʈʂóʊ kwân.ỳ]; born 30 May 1999) is a Chinese racing driver, who last competed in Formula One for Sauber. Born in Shanghai and raised in Sheffield, Zhou is the only Chinese driver to have started a Formula One Grand Prix.

Zhu Yuling (simplified Chinese:朱雨玲; traditional Chinese: 朱雨玲; born 10 January 1995 in Mianyang) is a Chinese table tennis player. International she was first active in 2010, where she won the World Championships in the youth field. At the Asian Championships in the same year Zhu vice-champion in the singles and doubles. Moreover she won silver at the Japan Open in the singles and at the Australian Open silver in the doubles. This medals were her first at the World Tour. After coming on place 105 in the world rankings in July, she was in September on place 25. In the years after that she got numerous medals at Junior World-and Asian championships. In 2013, her activity continued to increase. At the World Championships Zhu won two bronze medals. In the singles and in the doubles. At the end of the year she took part in the World Tour Grand Finals, where she lost to Li Xiaoxia in the quarter finals. In 2014, Zhu won gold with the team at the World Championships. Also she won the Swedish Open and the Kuwait Open. In 2015, she lost to Liu Shiwen in the quarterfinals at the World Championships, but she won gold with her in the doubles. At the Asian Championships she took gold. Because of the third place at the Asian Cup in the singles she took part at the World Cup, where she lost in the quarterfinals against Li Jiao. At the Grand Finals she won bronze in the singles and gold in the doubles. In 2016, followed one more time gold at the World Championships with the team as gold as the Grand Finals for the first time in the singles category. In 2017, she won bronze at the Asian Championships. But she won silver at the World Championships in the singles and in the doubles, too. In September and October she beat twice Liu Shiwen at the World Cup and Asian Cup. Therefore she was for the first time number one.
Ziaeddin Shademan (27 November 1923 – 12 March 2009) was an Iranian basketball player and politician. He competed at the 1948 Summer Olympics. From 1963 to 1965, he was the Mayor of Tehran.

He is considered to be one of the greatest players of all time. Zico is also widely known as the greatest Brazilian footballer to never win the World Cup. Parke Gerald Zinzan "Zin" Harris (18 July 1927 - 1 December 1991) was a New Zealand cricket player. He played nine Test matches between 1955 and 1965. Harris was a member of the New Zealand national cricket team. When they played against the South Africa national cricket team in 1961 to 1962, they reached a two-all draw in a five-match series. Harris was New Zealand's top scoring player in their Third Test of the series at Cape Town in South Africa. It was New Zealand's first overseas Test cricket victory. Harris had two sons. They are both former first-class cricket players. Chris Harris played for New Zealand and Ben Harris played for Canterbury and Otago. Both of Harris' sons also have Zinzan as a middle name.

Zinedine Zidane (born 23 June 1972, nicknamed Zizou, Yaz and ZZ) is a French former football player. He played for four European clubs and the French national team. He played for Real Madrid from 1997 to 2002. His name is a predecessor to Zedan. Zidane was born in Marseille, France and is of Kabyle Berber descent. Zidane played for several famous football clubs, like Juventus of Italy and Real Madrid of Spain. He led France to win the 1998 FIFA World Cup and the 2000 European Football Championship. In 2002 he also won the UEFA Champions League for Real Madrid, which was the ninth championship for Real Madrid. Zidane was picked as the FIFA World Player of the Year three times. He led France to the 2006 World Cup final and was arguably the best player in the tournament. He is widely regarded to be one of the greatest players of his generation and of all time. In 2006, Zidane announced that he would retire after the World Cup. Zidane was famous for headbutting Marco Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 FIFA World Cup final at the 110th minute of extra time and was sent off with a red card. France eventually lost 5-3 in penalties to Italy and got second place. This incident was widely known as the Zidane headbutt. There is even a sculpture of it in Doha, Qatar. Zion Lateef Williamson (born July 6, 2000) is an American professional basketball player for the New Orleans Pelicans of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He plays in the power forward position. He used to play for the Duke University. He gained attention for his slam dunks. He was drafted by the Pelicans in the 1st pick of the 2019 NBA Draft. On July 23, 2019, Williamson signed a five-year, $75 million shoe deal with Air Jordan.

Murray Zinzan Valentine Brooke (born 14 February, 1965 in Waiuku, New Zealand) is a New Zealand rugby player who played 58 tests/100 games for New Zealand and Auckland in rugby. He is the older brother of Robin Brooke and is distantly related to Gerard Beale, Zin Harris and Chris Harris.

Zito (18 August 1932 – 14 June 2015) was a former Brazilian football player. He has played for Brazil national team. He was a highly intelligent player, known for his leadership, tackling, passing, dribbling, his ability to win back possesion and his distribution. A strong, commanding and influential midfielder, known for his leadership, Zito usually played in a supporting role as a wing-half or half-back, serving as a defensive foil to his more offensive minded teammates. Considered as one of the greatest midfielders in the world in his prime, he was regarded to be one of the biggest idols of Santos FC, the club he represented for years. His club career was spent mostly in the service of Santos, captaining a side including Pelé to domestic and international successes. He was also part of the Brazilian squads which won the World Cup in 1958 and 1962. After his retirement as a player, Zito remained at Santos as a director and youth coordinator, developing several young future international players. Born in Roseira, São Paulo, Zito initially intended to become a schoolteacher, and attended technical schools in his hometown, before pursuing a career as a footballer. Zito joined Santos in 1952, after finishing his formation at hometown amateur club Roseira FC, and spending two years at Taubaté. He made his debut for Peixe on 29 June 1952 in a 3–1 friendly win against Madureira. Zito appeared regularly for Santos in the following 15 years, playing 727 games and scoring 57 goals. He was the captain of the Os Santásticos team of the late 1950s and 1960s, playing alongside Pelé, Pepe and other Brazilian stars. Zito was nicknamed Gerente (manager in Portuguese) by the media during his playing days, due to helping the manager Lula while outfields. Despite missing the two last games of 1963 Intercontinental Cup due to an injury, he acted as Lula's assistant during both matches as his team won the second title in a row. Zito played his last match on 7 November 1967, a 5–0 win against a mix between Ferroviário and Fortaleza at the Estádio Presidente Vargas. At international level, he earned 52 caps and scored 3 goals for Brazil. Zito made his for the national team in 1955. He was selected to play for Copa América in 1956, Brazil had an unsuccessful tournament and finished fourth. In 1957 he was selected again for the Copa América where Brazil finished as runners-up where he showed his great style of play, he was renowned as a playmaker and a incredible passer and a good dribbler. He partnered Didi in midfield duo, and was part of the squad which won the 1958 FIFA World Cup Final against hosts Sweden; after starting the tournament as a reserve, he finished it as an undisputed starter. In 1959 edition of Copa América Zito was called up, Brazil ended up as runners-up again and they were undefeated. In the 1962 edition in Chile, he was named in the Team of the Tournament. In the 1962 FIFA World Cup Final, Zito headed Brazil into the lead as they came from behind to win 3–1 against Czechoslovakia with Pelé absent through injury. Zito was called up to play during 1966 FIFA World Cup but he was unable to play and Brazil were eliminated after a 2-0 victory against Bulgaria and 3-1 defeat against Hungary and Portugal, Zito never played for Brazil again after the elimination. After retiring Zito was a vice-president at Santos between 1978 and 1982. After one year away from the club, he was named director of football by president Milton Teixeira, but left the post in 1987. In 2000, he was named a youth coordinate, helping the club to promote youngsters Robinho and Diego to the first team. Zito was credited with bringing 11-year-old Neymar to the club in 2003. With Gabriel, he was also the scout who saw the player and brought him to the club's youth system. Zito suffered from Alzheimer's disease and had memory lapses. Following a stroke the year before, Zito died on 14 June 2015 aged 82 in Santos, São Paulo, leaving Pelé, Pepe and Zagallo as the last three living Brazilian veterans of the 1958 World Cup final. In his honour, Santos decided to use the "Z" letter in the captain's armband (instead of the regular "C" used by most teams) from 2015 onwards.
